title.zh: 卷三百七十八 列傳第一百三十七 衞膚敏 劉珏 胡舜陟 沈晦 劉一止 胡交修 綦崇禮
title.en: Volume 378 Biographies 137: Wei Fumin, Liu Jue, Hu Shunzhi, Shen Hui, Liu Yizhi, Hu Jiaoxiu, Qi Chongli
title.raw: 卷三百七十八 列傳第一百三十七 衞膚敏 劉珏 胡舜陟 沈晦 劉一止 胡交修 綦崇禮 Volume 378 Biographies 137: Wei Fumin, Liu Jue, Hu Shunzhi, Shen Hui, Liu Yizhi, Hu Jiaoxiu, Qi Chongli

sentences.zh: 衛膚敏

translations.literal: Wei Fumin
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fumin

sentences.zh: 衛膚敏，字商彥，華亭人。

translations.literal: Wei Fumin, courtesy name Shangyan, was a native of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fumin, styled Shangyan, came from Huating.

sentences.zh: 以上舍生登宣和元年進士第，授文林郎、南京宗子博士，尋改教授。

translations.literal: As a shangshe student he passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Xuanhe, was appointed Wenlin Lang and Doctor of the Southern Capital Imperial Clan Directorate, and soon was changed to instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Having graduated as a shangshe student, he passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Xuanhe reign (1119) and was appointed Wenlin Lang and Doctor of the Southern Capital Imperial Clan Directorate; he was soon reassigned as an instructor.

sentences.zh: 六年，召對，改宣教郎、秘書省校書郎，命假給事中賀金主生辰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned for an audience, was changed to Xuanjiao Lang and collator in the Secretariat, and was ordered to serve temporarily as Supervising Censor to congratulate the Jin ruler on his birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1124) he was called to court, promoted to Xuanjiao Lang and collator in the Secretariat, and appointed acting Supervising Censor to convey birthday felicitations to the Jin sovereign.

sentences.zh: 膚敏奏曰：「彼生辰後天寧節五日，金人未聞入賀，而反先之以失國體，萬一金使不來，為朝廷羞。

translations.literal: Fumin memorialized, saying: "Their birthday comes five days after our Tianning Festival. The Jin have not been heard to send congratulations, yet we would go first and lose national dignity. If by any chance the Jin envoys do not come, it will be a disgrace to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Fumin submitted a memorial: "Their ruler's birthday falls five days after our Tianning Festival. We have not heard that the Jin intend to send felicitations, yet we would go first and compromise our national dignity. If the Jin envoys fail to appear, the court will suffer humiliation.

sentences.zh: 請至燕山候之，彼若不來，則以幣置境上而已。」

translations.literal: I ask that we proceed only as far as Yanshan and wait there. If they do not come, we need only leave the gifts at the border."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that we advance only to Yanshan and wait. If they do not come, we can simply leave the tribute gifts at the frontier and return."

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 既至燕，金賀使果不至，遂置幣而返。

translations.literal: When he reached Yan, the Jin congratulatory envoy indeed did not arrive, so he left the gifts and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Yan, he found that no Jin congratulatory mission had come. He left the gifts and returned.

sentences.zh: 七年，復假給事中以行，及慶源府，逢許亢宗還，語金國事，曰：「彼且大入，其勢不可往。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again served temporarily as Supervising Censor on the mission. When he reached Qingyuan Prefecture he met Xu Kangzong returning, who spoke of Jin affairs and said: "They are about to invade on a large scale. The situation makes it impossible to go."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1125) he again served as acting Supervising Censor on the mission. At Qingyuan Prefecture he met Xu Kangzong returning from the north, who warned of Jin affairs: "They are poised for a major invasion. Under these circumstances you cannot proceed."

sentences.zh: 膚敏至燕，報愈急，眾懼不敢進，膚敏叱曰：「吾將君命以行，其可止乎？」

translations.literal: When Fumin reached Yan the reports grew ever more urgent. The party feared and dared not advance. Fumin rebuked them, saying: "I bear the ruler's commission. How can we stop?"
translations.idiomatic: When Fumin reached Yan, the intelligence grew more alarming by the day. His companions were afraid to go forward. Fumin rebuked them: "I carry the sovereign's commission. How can we turn back?"

sentences.zh: 即至金國，知其兵已舉，殊不為屈。

translations.literal: He thereupon proceeded to the Jin state, knowing their armies had already been mobilized, yet he was not cowed in the least.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on into Jin territory. Though he knew their armies were already in motion, he did not yield an inch.

sentences.zh: 及將還，金人所答國書，欲以押字代璽，膚敏力爭曰：「押字豈所以交鄰國。」

translations.literal: When he was about to return, the Jin reply to the state letter sought to use a signature stamp in place of the imperial seal. Fumin argued forcefully: "How can a signature stamp be the way to communicate with a neighboring state?"
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to return, the Jin sought to affix a personal signature stamp to their reply rather than the imperial seal. Fumin protested vigorously: "A signature stamp is no way to conduct diplomacy between neighboring states."

sentences.zh: 論難往復，卒易以璽。

translations.literal: After repeated debate back and forth, they finally changed it to the seal.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged argument, they finally substituted the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 及受書，欲令雙跪，膚敏曰：「雙跪乃北朝禮，安可令南朝人行之哉！」

translations.literal: When he was to receive the letter they wished to make him kneel on both knees. Fumin said: "Kneeling on both knees is the ritual of the northern court. How can the southern court be made to perform it!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was to receive the letter, they demanded that he kneel on both knees. Fumin said: "The double kneel is northern ritual. How can subjects of the southern court be made to observe it!"

sentences.zh: 爭辨逾時，卒單跪以受。

translations.literal: After disputing for a long time, he finally received it kneeling on one knee.
translations.idiomatic: After a protracted dispute, he finally received the document kneeling on one knee only.

sentences.zh: 金人積不說，中道羈留且半年。

translations.literal: The Jin had long been displeased with him and detained him en route for nearly half a year.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, who had long resented him, detained him midway for nearly six months.

sentences.zh: 至涿州新城，與斡離不遇，遣人約相見，拒之不可，遂語之曰：「必欲相見，其禮當如何？」

translations.literal: When he reached Xincheng in Zhuo Prefecture he encountered Wanyan Zonghan, who sent someone to arrange a meeting. Fumin refused and could not be moved, then said to them: "If you insist on meeting, what ritual should be observed?"
translations.idiomatic: At Xincheng in Zhuo Prefecture he encountered Wanyan Zonghan, who sent an envoy to arrange a meeting. Fumin refused. When pressed, he asked: "If you insist on a meeting, what form of ceremony do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「有例。」

translations.literal: They said: "There is precedent."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "There is precedent."

sentences.zh: 膚敏笑曰：「例謂趨伏羅拜，此禮焉可用？

translations.literal: Fumin laughed and said: "Precedent means rushing forward, prostrating, and bowing in the Luo style. How can such a ritual be used?
translations.idiomatic: Fumin laughed. "Your precedent means rushing forward and prostrating in the Luo bow. What use is such a ceremony?

sentences.zh: 北朝止一君耳，皇子郎君雖貴，人臣也，一介之使雖賤，亦人臣也。

translations.literal: The northern court has only one sovereign. Princes and noble lords, though exalted, are subjects; a single envoy, though lowly, is also a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The northern realm has but one sovereign. Princes and noble lords, however exalted, are subjects; an envoy, however humble, is likewise a subject.

sentences.zh: 兩國之臣相見，而用君臣之禮，是北朝一國有二君也。」

translations.literal: For subjects of two states to meet and use the ritual between sovereign and subject would mean the northern court had two sovereigns in one realm."
translations.idiomatic: If subjects of two states meet using sovereign-and-subject ritual, you would have two sovereigns in one realm."

sentences.zh: 金人氣折，始曰：「唯所欲。」

translations.literal: The Jin were overawed and at last said: "As you wish."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were silenced and at last said: "As you wish."

sentences.zh: 膚敏長揖而入。

translations.literal: Fumin made a long bow and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Fumin entered with a formal bow.

sentences.zh: 既坐，金人出誓書示之，膚敏卻不視，曰：「遠使久不聞朝廷事，此書真偽不可知。」

translations.literal: Once seated, the Jin produced an oath document to show him. Fumin turned away and would not look, saying: "A distant envoy has long been out of touch with court affairs. Whether this document is genuine cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, the Jin produced an oath document for his inspection. Fumin refused to look at it. "A distant envoy has long been out of touch with court affairs," he said. "I cannot know whether this document is genuine."

sentences.zh: 因論用兵事，又以語折之，幾復為所留。

translations.literal: He then discussed military affairs and again refuted them with his words, and was nearly detained once more.
translations.idiomatic: He then debated military affairs and again bested them in argument, nearly being detained a second time.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，始還，進三官，遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era he at last returned, was advanced three ranks, and was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Jingkang crisis (1126) he finally returned, was promoted three ranks, and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會高麗遣使來賀，命假太常少卿往接之。

translations.literal: When Goryeo sent envoys to offer congratulations, he was ordered to serve temporarily as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo dispatched envoys with congratulations, he was appointed acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to receive them.

sentences.zh: 朝論欲改稱宣問使，膚敏曰：「國家厚遇高麗久矣，今邊事方作，不可遽削其禮，失遠人心，願姑仍舊。」

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to change the title to Inquiry Commissioner. Fumin said: "The state has long treated Goryeo generously. Border affairs are just now arising; we cannot abruptly reduce their ceremonial treatment and lose the hearts of distant peoples. I ask that we provisionally keep the old usage."
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion favored renaming the post Inquiry Commissioner. Fumin objected: "The court has long treated Goryeo with generosity. With border troubles just erupting, we must not abruptly curtail their ceremonial standing and alienate distant allies. I ask that the former title be retained for now."

sentences.zh: 乃復稱接伴使。

translations.literal: The title Reception Commissioner was therefore restored.
translations.idiomatic: The title was accordingly restored to Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既至明州，會京師多難，乃便宜稱詔厚賜使者，遣還。

translations.literal: When he reached Ming Prefecture, the capital was in great turmoil, so he exercised discretionary authority, proclaimed an edict in the emperor's name granting the envoys generous gifts, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Ming Prefecture he learned that the capital was in crisis. Exercising discretionary authority, he issued a proclamation in the emperor's name granting the envoys generous gifts and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，言：「前日金人憑陵，都邑失守，朝臣欲存趙氏者不過一二人而已，其他皆屈節受辱，不以為恥，甚者為敵人斂金帛，索妃嬪，無所不至，求其能詐楚如紀信者無有也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Diarist and said: "When the Jin lately overran us and the capital fell, of court officials who wished to preserve the Zhao house there were no more than one or two. The rest all submitted and suffered humiliation without shame; the worst collected gold and silk for the enemy and demanded imperial consorts—nothing was beyond them. One searches in vain for anyone who deceived Chu as Ji Xin did.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Attendant Diarist, he memorialized: "When the Jin overran the realm and the capital fell, scarcely one or two officials sought to preserve the Zhao dynasty. The rest submitted to humiliation without shame; the worst collected gold and silk for the enemy and demanded imperial consorts—nothing was beyond them. Not one could be found to match Ji Xin's ruse against Chu.

sentences.zh: 及金人偽立叛臣，僭竊位號，在廷之臣逃避不從及約寇退歸位趙氏者，不過一二人而已，其他皆委質求榮，不以為愧，甚者為叛臣稱功德，說符命，主推戴之議，草勸進之文，無所不為，求其擊朱泚如段秀實者無有也。

translations.literal: When the Jin falsely installed a rebel minister and usurped the throne title, of officials at court who fled and refused to follow, or who pledged that when the invaders withdrew they would restore the Zhao house, there were no more than one or two. The rest all submitted and sought glory without shame; the worst praised the rebel minister's merit, expounded portents, led the movement to enthrone him, and drafted documents urging his accession—nothing was left undone. One searches in vain for anyone who struck down Zhu Ci as Duan Xiushi did.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin installed a puppet ruler and usurped the imperial title, scarcely one or two officials at court refused to serve or pledged to restore the Zhao house once the invaders withdrew. The rest submitted for advancement without shame; the worst praised the puppet's virtues, expounded portents, led the movement to enthrone him, and drafted accession memorials. Not one could be found to match Duan Xiushi's strike against Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 今陛下踐祚之初，苟無典刑，何以立國？

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, if there is no penal code, how can the state be established?
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Your Majesty's reign, if there is no exemplary punishment, how can the state endure?

sentences.zh: 凡前日屈節敵人，委質偽命者，宜差第其罪，大則族，次則誅，又其次竄殛，下則斥之遠方，終身不齒，豈可猶畀祠祿，使塵班列哉？」

translations.literal: All who formerly submitted to the enemy or pledged themselves to the false regime should have their crimes ranked in degrees: the greatest punished by extinction of the clan, next by execution, next by exile or death by strangulation, and the least expelled to distant regions and never again counted among officials. How can they still be granted sacrificial stipends and allowed to pollute the court ranks?"
translations.idiomatic: All who submitted to the enemy or served the puppet regime should be punished in graduated degrees: the gravest by clan extinction, next by execution, then by exile or strangulation, and the least banished forever from office. How can they still receive stipends and sit among the court ranks?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「今二帝北遷，寰宇痛心，願陛下愈自貶損，不忘服雪，卑宮室，菲飲食，惡衣服，減嬪御，斥聲樂，以至歲時上壽，春秋錫宴，一切罷之，雖饗郊廟亦不用樂。

translations.literal: He also said: "Now that the two emperors have been taken north, all under Heaven is stricken with grief. I hope Your Majesty will further abase yourself, never forget to wear mourning for their redemption, make your palaces humble, your food plain, your garments coarse, reduce the consorts, banish music and entertainment—even birthday felicitations and spring and autumn banquets should all be abolished; even at suburban and ancestral sacrifices let no music be used.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "With both emperors captive in the north, the realm grieves. I urge Your Majesty to humble yourself further: wear mourning for their redemption, dwell in modest quarters, eat plain food, dress in coarse garments, reduce the harem, banish music—even birthday felicitations and seasonal banquets should cease, and even suburban and ancestral rites should be performed without music.

sentences.zh: 必俟兩宮還闕，然後復常，庶幾精誠昭格天地，感動人心。」

translations.literal: Only when the two palaces return to the capital should normal practice be restored, so that sincerity may move Heaven and Earth and touch the hearts of the people."
translations.idiomatic: Only when both sovereigns return to the capital should normal practice resume, so that sincerity may move Heaven and Earth and stir the hearts of the people."

sentences.zh: 拜右諫議大夫兼侍讀，言：「行在頗興土木之役，非所以示四方，乞罷築承慶院、昇暘宮。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, and said: "The mobile court is undertaking considerable construction, which is not the way to show the four quarters. I beg that construction of Chengqing Court and Shengyang Palace be halted."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, he urged: "The mobile court is undertaking extensive construction, which sends the wrong signal to the realm. I beg that work on Chengqing Court and Shengyang Palace be halted."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「“凡黜陟自中出者，皆由三省乃得奉行，或戾祖宗成憲者，皆許執奏。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "All dismissals and appointments issued from the inner palace must pass through the Three Departments before they may be carried out; whenever they violate the established statutes of the ancestors, remonstrance memorials should be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized: "All appointments and dismissals issued from the inner palace must pass through the Three Departments before taking effect; whenever they violate ancestral statutes, officials should be permitted to remonstrate."

sentences.zh: 時內侍李志道以赦恩復保慶軍承宣使，添差入內都知，膚敏極論罷之。

translations.literal: At that time the inner attendant Li Zhidao, through an amnesty, was restored as Commissioner of the Baoqing Army and given an additional assignment as Director of the Inner Palace. Fumin argued forcefully until the appointment was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch Li Zhidao was restored through an amnesty to Commissioner of the Baoqing Army with an additional post as Director of the Inner Palace. Fumin argued vigorously until the appointment was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 初，欽宗內侍昭慶軍承宣使容機，圍城中時乞致仕，高宗即位，命起之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the inner attendant of Emperor Qinzong, Commissioner of the Zhaoqing Army Rong Ji, had requested retirement during the siege of the capital. When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he was ordered to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Qinzong's eunuch Rong Ji, Commissioner of the Zhaoqing Army, had requested retirement during the siege. When Gaozong acceded, he was ordered to resume office.

sentences.zh: 膚敏言：「自古帝王未有求閹寺於閑退而用者。」

translations.literal: Fumin said: "From antiquity no sovereign has ever sought out a eunuch in retirement for employment."
translations.idiomatic: Fumin objected: "No sovereign in history has ever recalled a eunuch from retirement for service."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 后父邢煥除徽猷閣待制，太后兄子孟忠厚顯謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: The empress's father Xing Huan was appointed Awaiting Draftsman of the Huiyou Pavilion; the empress dowager's nephew Meng Zhonghou was made Academician Expositor of the Xianmo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Xing Huan was appointed Awaiting Draftsman of the Huiyou Pavilion; the empress dowager's nephew Meng Zhonghou was made Academician Expositor of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 膚敏言：「非祖宗法。」

translations.literal: Fumin said: "This is not ancestral law."
translations.idiomatic: Fumin protested: "This violates ancestral precedent."

sentences.zh: 煥尋換武職，忠厚自若。

translations.literal: Huan was soon transferred to a military post, but Zhonghou remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was soon transferred to a military post, but Zhonghou's appointment stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 俄遷膚敏中書舍人，膚敏懇奏曰：「昔司馬光論張方平不當參知政事，自御史中丞遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon Fumin was transferred to Secretariat Drafter. Fumin earnestly memorialized: "In former times Sima Guang argued that Zhang Fangping should not serve as Vice Grand Councilor when he was moved from Censor-in-Chief to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fumin was promoted to Secretariat Drafter. He submitted an earnest memorial: "When Sima Guang argued that Zhang Fangping was unfit for the vice premiership, Fangping had been moved from Censor-in-Chief to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 光言：『以臣為是，則方平當罷；

translations.literal: Guang said: "If I am right, Fangping should be dismissed;"
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "If I am right, Fangping should be dismissed;"

sentences.zh: 以臣為非，則臣當貶。

translations.literal: if I am wrong, I should be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: if I am wrong, I should be demoted.

sentences.zh: 今兩無所問而遷臣，臣所未諭。』

translations.literal: Now with neither question answered I am promoted—this I do not understand."
translations.idiomatic: Yet with neither question resolved I am promoted. I cannot understand this."

sentences.zh: 臣雖不肖，願附于司馬光。」

translations.literal: Though I am unworthy, I wish to attach myself to Sima Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy though I am, I would follow Sima Guang's example."

sentences.zh: 又言：「事母后莫若孝，待戚屬莫若恩，勸臣下莫若賞。

translations.literal: He also said: "In serving the empress dowager nothing surpasses filial piety; in treating kinsmen nothing surpasses kindness; in encouraging officials nothing surpasses reward.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In serving the empress dowager, nothing surpasses filial piety; in treating kinsmen, nothing surpasses kindness; in encouraging officials, nothing surpasses reward.

sentences.zh: 今陛下順太母以非法，非所謂孝，處忠厚以非分，非所謂恩，不用臣言而遷其官，非所謂賞，一舉而三失矣。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty complies with the grand empress dowager unlawfully—that is not what is called filial piety; you treat Zhonghou beyond his proper station—that is not what is called kindness; you promote his office without heeding my words—that is not what is called reward. In one act you have committed three failures."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty indulges the grand empress dowager unlawfully—that is not filial piety; you favor Zhonghou beyond his station—that is not kindness; you promote him without heeding my counsel—that is not reward. In a single act you have committed three errors."

sentences.zh: 帝命宰相諭膚敏曰：「朝廷以次遷官，非因論事也。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief councilor to inform Fumin: "The court promotes by seniority in rank; it is not because of your remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed the chief councilor to explain to Fumin: "This promotion follows ordinary seniority; it is not a response to your memorial."

sentences.zh: 膚敏猶不拜，居家逾月，及忠厚改承宣使，詔后族勿除從官，膚敏始拜命。

translations.literal: Fumin still refused to accept the appointment and remained at home for more than a month. When Zhonghou was changed to Commissioner and an edict forbade appointing empress clansmen to attendant posts, Fumin at last accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Fumin still refused to accept and remained at home for over a month. Only when Zhonghou was demoted to Commissioner and an edict barred empress clansmen from attendant posts did Fumin finally accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 又言：「中書根本之地，舍人所掌，不特演綸而已。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Secretariat is the root of government. What the drafters administer is not merely the drafting of edicts."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Secretariat is the foundation of government. The drafter's charge is not merely to compose edicts."

sentences.zh: 凡命令不合公議者，率封還之。

translations.literal: Whenever an order did not accord with public opinion, he invariably sealed it and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an order conflicted with public opinion, he invariably sealed it and returned it unapproved.

sentences.zh: 會膚敏知貢舉，有進士何烈對省試策，謬稱「臣」，諫官李處遯乞正考官鹵莽之罪，以集英殿修撰提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: When Fumin served as chief examiner, the jinshi He Lie in answering the metropolitan examination policy essay wrongly styled himself "your subject." The remonstrance official Li Chudun asked that the chief examiner be punished for carelessness, and Fumin was made Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Excellence and Administrator of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Fumin served as chief examiner, the candidate He Lie wrongly styled himself "your subject" in the policy examination. Remonstrance official Li Chudun called for punishing the chief examiner's negligence, and Fumin was reassigned as Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Excellence with charge of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 或謂膚敏在後省論事，為黃潛善、汪伯彥所惡，故因事斥之。

translations.literal: Some said that because Fumin remonstrated in the Secretariat he was hated by Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, and was therefore dismissed on this pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that Fumin's remonstrances in the Secretariat had earned the enmity of Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, who used this incident to remove him.

sentences.zh: 三年春，召赴行在。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year (1129) he was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時帝次平江。

translations.literal: The emperor was then stationed at Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 膚敏入見，言及時事泣下，帝亦泣曰：「卿今宜知無不言，有請不以時對。」

translations.literal: Fumin entered audience; speaking of current affairs he wept. The emperor also wept and said: "You should now know there is nothing you may not say. If you have a request, do not fail to speak in timely fashion."
translations.idiomatic: Fumin had an audience. As he spoke of current affairs he wept, and the emperor wept as well. "You must speak freely hereafter," the emperor said. "If you have counsel, do not withhold it."

sentences.zh: 膚敏謝曰：「臣頃嘗三為陛下言，揚州非駐蹕之地，乞早幸江寧。

translations.literal: Fumin replied in thanks: "Your subject has thrice told Your Majesty that Yangzhou is no place for the imperial encampment, and begged an early move to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Fumin replied: "I have thrice urged that Yangzhou is unsuitable as an imperial residence and begged an early move to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 今錢塘亦非帝王之都，宜須事定，亟還金陵。」

translations.literal: Now Qiantang is also no capital for an emperor. When affairs are settled you should swiftly return to Jinling."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang is likewise no fit capital. Once affairs stabilize, Your Majesty should return swiftly to Jinling."

sentences.zh: 因陳所以守長江之策，帝善其言。

translations.literal: He then set forth his strategy for defending the Yangzi, and the emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented his strategy for defending the Yangzi, which the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 翌日，再對，歸得疾，然猶力疾扈蹕至臨安。

translations.literal: The next day he had a second audience. Returning he fell ill, yet he still forced himself through illness to escort the imperial procession to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he had a second audience. He fell ill on his return but still forced himself to escort the imperial procession to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 俄除刑部侍郎，未拜，謁告歸華亭就醫，許之，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice but had not yet accepted the commission when he requested leave to return to Huating for medical treatment. This was granted, and he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of Justice but had not yet assumed the post when he requested leave to seek treatment in Huating. Permission was granted, and he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，膚敏久疾臥舟中，不能朝，時苗、劉之變，帝未反正，宰相朱勝非言于隆祐太后，以「膚敏稱疾坐觀成敗，無人臣節」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fumin had long been ill and lay in his boat unable to attend court. During the Miao-Liu mutiny, before the emperor had been restored, Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei said to Empress Dowager Longyou that "Fumin feigned illness and sat watching the outcome without the integrity of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Miao-Liu mutiny, Fumin had lain gravely ill in his boat and could not attend court. Before the emperor was restored, Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei told Empress Dowager Longyou that Fumin "feigned illness and watched events unfold without a subject's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 及卒，始明其非偽云。

translations.literal: When he died it became clear his illness had not been feigned.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his death was it understood that his illness had been genuine.

sentences.zh: 年四十九，特贈大中大夫。

translations.literal: He was forty-nine years old and was specially posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-nine. He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 子仲英、仲傑、仲循。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhongying, Zhongjie, and Zhongxun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhongying, Zhongjie, and Zhongxun.

sentences.zh: 劉珏，字希范，湖州長興人。

translations.literal: Liu Jue, courtesy name Xifan, was a native of Changxing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jue, styled Xifan, came from Changxing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Chongning reign (1106).

sentences.zh: 初遊太學，以書遺中書舍人鄒浩曰：「公始為博士論取士之失，免所居官，在諫省斥宮掖之非，遠遷嶺表，豈逆計禍福，邀後日報哉，固欲蹈古人行也。

translations.literal: When he first studied at the Imperial University he sent a letter to Secretariat Drafter Zou Hao, saying: "When you were first a Erudite you discussed errors in the selection of scholars and were dismissed from your post; in the Remonstrance Bureau you denounced wrongdoing in the palace women and were exiled far to the southern marches. Did you calculate fortune and misfortune in advance to invite later reward? You wished to follow the conduct of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Imperial University he wrote to Secretariat Drafter Zou Hao: "As an Erudite you criticized errors in civil service examinations and lost your post; in the Remonstrance Bureau you denounced palace abuses and were exiled to the far south. You did not calculate fortune and misfortune to win later reward—you sought to follow the ancients' example.

sentences.zh: 今庶政豈盡修明，百官豈盡忠實，從臣繼去，豈盡非才，言官屢逐，豈盡有罪！

translations.literal: Are all affairs of state now fully well governed? Are all officials fully loyal and honest? As attendant ministers leave one after another, were they all without talent? As remonstrance officials are repeatedly expelled, were they all guilty?
translations.idiomatic: Are state affairs fully well governed? Are all officials loyal and honest? As attendant ministers depart in succession, were none of them talented? As remonstrance officials are repeatedly expelled, were all of them guilty?

sentences.zh: 信任逾曩昔而拱默不言，天下之士竊有疑焉，願有以慰塞群望。」

translations.literal: Yet trust exceeds former times while you remain silent. Scholars throughout the realm privately harbor doubts. I hope you will find some way to satisfy and fulfill the hopes of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you enjoy greater trust than ever while remaining silent. Scholars throughout the realm privately wonder. I hope you will find some way to answer their expectations."

sentences.zh: 浩得書愧謝之。

translations.literal: Hao received the letter and thanked him in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Hao received the letter and thanked him with remorse.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，擢監察御史，坐言事知舒州，留為尚書主客員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe he was promoted to Investigating Censor; for remonstrance he was made prefect of Shuzhou but was retained as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Host-Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe (1122) he was promoted to Investigating Censor. For his remonstrances he was appointed prefect of Shuzhou but was retained as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Host-Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 陳十開端之戒曰：

translations.literal: He set forth ten warnings of beginnings, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He presented ten warnings about dangerous beginnings:

sentences.zh: 「陛下即位罷御筆，止營繕，登俊乂，詘虛誕，戢內侍之權，開言者之路，命令既當，未嘗數改，任用既公，率皆稱職，賞必視功，政必核實，此天下所以指日而徯太平也。

translations.literal: "When Your Majesty acceded you abolished imperial brush edicts, halted construction, elevated the worthy, repressed empty boasting, restrained the power of inner attendants, and opened the path for remonstrance. Orders were fitting and never repeatedly changed; appointments were fair and all largely fulfilled their duties; rewards were tied to merit and governance was verified in fact. For this the realm looked day by day toward peace.
translations.idiomatic: "At Your Majesty's accession you abolished imperial brush edicts, halted construction, elevated the worthy, repressed empty boasting, restrained eunuch power, and opened the path for remonstrance. Orders were sound and seldom changed; appointments were fair and officials largely performed their duties; rewards followed merit and governance was verified in practice. The realm looked to peace with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 比者內降數出，三省罕有可否，此御筆之開端也。

translations.literal: Lately inner edicts have issued repeatedly and the Three Departments rarely approve or disapprove—this is the beginning of imperial brush edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Lately inner edicts have issued repeatedly while the Three Departments rarely approve or disapprove—this is the beginning of a return to brush edicts.

sentences.zh: 教子弟既有其所，又徹而新之，長入祗候之班，勢若可緩，亟而成之，此營繕之開端也。

translations.literal: Instruction of sons and younger brothers already had its place, yet buildings were torn down and rebuilt anew; long-service attendants entered the waiting ranks; the work seemed it could be delayed yet was rushed to completion—this is the beginning of construction.
translations.idiomatic: Schools for imperial clansmen already had quarters, yet buildings were torn down and rebuilt; long-service attendants were added to waiting ranks; work that seemed deferrable was rushed to completion—this is the beginning of renewed construction.

sentences.zh: 河陽付之庸才，涇原委之貪吏，此任用失當之開端也。

translations.literal: Heyang was entrusted to a mediocrity and Jingyuan to a greedy official—this is the beginning of improper appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang was entrusted to mediocrity and Jingyuan to a corrupt official—this is the beginning of improper appointments.

sentences.zh: 花石等濫賞，既治復止，馬忠統兵，累行累召，此命令數易之開端也。

translations.literal: Rewards for Huashi and the like were lavished; after punishment they were again halted. Ma Zhong commanded troops and was repeatedly sent forth and repeatedly recalled—this is the beginning of frequent changes in orders.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for the Huashi Bureau were lavished, then punished offenses were pardoned. Ma Zhong was repeatedly dispatched and recalled—this is the beginning of erratic commands.

sentences.zh: 三省、密院議論各有所見，啟擬各舉所知，持不同不比之說，忘同寅協恭之議，此大臣不和之開端也。

translations.literal: The Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs each held their own views in discussion; in memorials each recommended those they knew; they clung to differing opinions and refused comparison, forgetting the principle that colleagues should harmonize—this is the beginning of discord among great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs each held separate views; in memorials each recommended his own associates; they clung to differing opinions and forgot collegial harmony—this is the beginning of discord among chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 內路之帥擅作聖旨指揮，行郡之守稱為外任監當，此臣下誕謾之開端也。

translations.literal: Commanders of inner circuits arbitrarily issued orders in the name of imperial edicts; prefects of outer circuits were styled supervisors of external assignments—this is the beginning of officials' arrogance and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commanders arbitrarily issued orders in the emperor's name; prefects were styled supervisors of external assignments—this is the beginning of official arrogance and deceit.

sentences.zh: 董局務者廣辟官屬，侍帷幄者分爭殿廬，此內侍恣橫之開端也。

translations.literal: Those managing bureaus broadly expanded their staffs; those attending the imperial curtain disputed over palace chambers—this is the beginning of inner attendants' unrestrained arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau chiefs expanded their staffs without restraint; attendants at the imperial curtain disputed over palace quarters—this is the beginning of eunuch arrogance.

sentences.zh: 兩省繳奏多命以次行下，或戒以不得再繳，臺諫言事失當，率責為遠小監當，此言路壅塞之開端也。

translations.literal: Returned memorials from the Two Departments were often ordered issued in sequence, or officials were warned not to return them again. When censorate and remonstrance officials spoke inappropriately they were routinely punished with distant petty supervisory posts—this is the beginning of the blocking of the path of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Returned memorials from the Two Departments were often ordered issued without review, or officials were warned not to return them again. Censorate and remonstrance officials who erred were routinely banished to distant petty posts—this is the beginning of blocked remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 恤民之詔累下，未可行者多，是為空文無實德，此政事失信之開端也。

translations.literal: Edicts showing compassion for the people were repeatedly issued, yet many could not be carried out. These were empty words without real virtue—this is the beginning of loss of trust in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts showing compassion for the people were repeatedly issued, yet many could not be implemented. These were empty words without real effect—this is the beginning of lost credibility in governance.

sentences.zh: 隨龍第賞，冠帶之工亦推恩，金兵扣闕，禮房之吏亦進秩，此爵賞僣濫之開端也。

translations.literal: Rewards followed rank in the imperial entourage; even artisans of caps and belts received favor. When Jin troops reached the capital, clerks of the Rites Bureau also received promotion in rank—this is the beginning of excessive and improper enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards followed rank in the imperial entourage; even artisans of caps and belts received favors. When Jin troops reached the capital, clerks of the Rites Bureau were also promoted—this is the beginning of excessive and improper rewards.

sentences.zh: 是十者雖未若前日之甚，其端已見，杜而止之，可以馴致治平，因而循之，雖有智者不能善其後矣。」

translations.literal: These ten, though not yet as grave as in former days, already show their beginnings. Stop and block them and orderly peace may be gradually attained; if you follow them instead, even the wise cannot set things right afterward."
translations.idiomatic: These ten, though not yet as grave as before, already show their beginnings. Stop them now and orderly peace may still be attained; follow them further and even the wise cannot repair the damage."

sentences.zh: 詹度都堂稟議，中書舍人安扶持不可，改命珏書行，珏言：「伐燕之役，度以書贊童貫大舉，去秋蔡靖屢以金人點集為言，度獨謂不應有此，遂不設備，請竄度嶺表。」

translations.literal: Zhan Du submitted a proposal at the chief councilor's court. Secretariat Drafter An Fu held it unacceptable. The order was changed for Jue to draft and issue it. Jue said: "In the campaign against Yan, Du by letter praised Tong Guan's great undertaking. Last autumn Cai Jing repeatedly spoke of Jin troop mobilization, but Du alone said this should not be so and made no preparations. I ask that Du be exiled to the southern marches."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Du submitted a proposal at the chief councilor's court. Secretariat Drafter An Fu objected. The order was reassigned to Jue to draft. Jue argued: "In the campaign against Yan, Du praised Tong Guan's grand strategy in writing. Last autumn Cai Jing repeatedly warned of Jin troop mobilization, but Du alone dismissed the reports and made no preparations. I ask that Du be exiled to the southern marches."

sentences.zh: 詔予宮祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted him a palace temple post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Du a palace temple post.

sentences.zh: 李綱以觀文殿學士知揚州，安扶又持不可，珏言：「韓琦好水之敗，韓絳西州之敗，皆不免黜責。

translations.literal: Li Gang was made Academician at the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Yangzhou. An Fu again held it unacceptable. Jue said: "Han Qi's defeat at Haoshui and Han Jiang's defeat at Xizhou both could not escape demotion and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang was appointed Academician at the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Yangzhou. An Fu again objected. Jue argued: "Han Qi's defeat at Haoshui and Han Jiang's defeat at Xizhou both led to demotion and censure.

sentences.zh: 綱勇於報國，銳於用兵，聽用不審，數有敗衄，宜降黜以示懲戒。」

translations.literal: Gang is bold in serving the state and keen in employing troops, but he does not examine counsel carefully and has suffered repeated defeats. He should be demoted to show discipline."
translations.idiomatic: Gang is bold in serving the state and eager to employ troops, but he does not weigh counsel carefully and has suffered repeated defeats. He should be demoted as a warning."

sentences.zh: 綱改宮祠。

translations.literal: Gang was changed to a palace temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was reassigned to a palace temple post.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎馮澥言珏持兩端，為綱遊說，提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Feng Xi said Jue held both sides and lobbied for Gang, and he was made Administrator of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Feng Xi accused Jue of equivocating and lobbying for Gang. Jue was reassigned as Administrator of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，論內降、營繕二事曰：「陛下以前朝房院而建承慶院，議者以為營造浸廣，以隆祐太后時有御筆，議者以為內降數出。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor and discussed the two matters of inner edicts and construction, saying: "Your Majesty built Chengqing Court on the site of a former dynasty's palace compound, and critics held that construction was growing extensive; because Empress Dowager Longyou had issued brush edicts, critics held that inner edicts were issuing repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Supervising Censor, he addressed inner edicts and construction: "Your Majesty built Chengqing Court on the site of a former palace compound, and critics held that construction was expanding; because Empress Dowager Longyou had issued brush edicts, critics held that inner edicts were proliferating.

sentences.zh: 蓋除授不歸中書，工役領之內侍，此人言所以籍籍也。

translations.literal: The reason popular talk is so agitated is that appointments do not pass through the Secretariat and construction labor is directed by inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for public agitation is that appointments bypass the Secretariat and construction is directed by eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 營繕悉歸有司，中旨皆許執奏，則眾論息矣。」

translations.literal: If construction were entirely returned to the proper offices and inner edicts were all permitted to be returned with remonstrance, popular discussion would subside."
translations.idiomatic: If construction were returned to the proper offices and inner edicts were all subject to remonstrance, public criticism would subside."

sentences.zh: 孟忠厚除顯謨閣直學士，邢煥徽猷閣待制，珏封還，言舊制外戚未有為兩禁官者，詔煥換武階。

translations.literal: Meng Zhonghou was made Direct Academician at the Hall for Displaying Governance; Xing Huan was made Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning. Jue returned upon completing his mission and said that by old regulation no maternal relative had ever held Two Restricted Bureau posts. An edict ordered Xing Huan transferred to military rank.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhonghou was appointed Direct Academician at the Hall for Displaying Governance and Xing Huan Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning. When Jue returned from his mission he observed that precedent never allowed imperial in-laws to hold posts in the Two Restricted Bureaus. The throne ordered Xing Huan transferred to a military commission.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「忠厚乃隆祐太后族，宜體朕優奉太后之意。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhonghou is of Empress Dowager Longyou's clan; you should reflect my intent to honor the empress dowager generously."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhonghou belongs to Empress Dowager Longyou's clan. You should respect my wish to treat the empress dowager with generous favor."

sentences.zh: 珏持益堅，忠厚尋亦換武階。

translations.literal: Jue held his position all the more firmly, and Zhonghou soon also was transferred to military rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jue held firm, and before long Zhonghou too was transferred to a military commission.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，同修國史，言：「淮甸備敵，兵食為先，今以降卒為見兵，以糴本為見糧，無一可恃，維揚城池未修，軍旅多闕，卒有不虞，何以待之？」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and Associate Compiler of the National History, saying: "In the Huai region's preparations against the enemy, troops and provisions come first. Now surrendered soldiers serve as the troops on the rolls and grain-purchase funds as the provisions on the rolls—nothing can be relied upon. Yangzhou's walls are unrepaired and the army lacks many men. If the unexpected occurs, how shall we respond?"
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Vice Minister of Personnel and Associate Compiler of the National History, he memorialized: "Defense of the Huai region depends first on troops and grain. Today surrendered soldiers pass as our standing army and purchase funds pass as stored grain—neither can be trusted. Yangzhou's walls remain unrepaired and ranks are badly depleted. If disaster strikes, what then?"

sentences.zh: 已而金人果乘虛大入，帝亟如臨安，以珏為龍圖閣直學士、知宣州。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens indeed seized the opportunity and invaded on a large scale. The emperor hastened to Lin'an and made Jue Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Designs and prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens soon exploited the opening and swept in. The emperor rushed to Lin'an and appointed Jue Direct Academician at the Hall of Dragon Designs and prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄復為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以久雨詔求言，珏疏論消天變、收人心數事，詞極激切，並陳荊、陝、江、淮守禦之略：「願申詔大臣，悉屏細務，唯謀守禦。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged rain an edict sought remonstrance. Jue memorialized on several matters for dispelling heaven's portents and winning hearts—his language extremely sharp—and also set forth plans for defending Jing, Shaanxi, the Yangtze, and the Huai: "I wish Your Majesty would reissue edicts to great ministers to put aside minor affairs and devote themselves solely to planning defense.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged rain the throne called for counsel. Jue submitted a sharp memorial on dispelling heaven's warnings and winning hearts, and laid out plans to defend Jing, Shaanxi, the Yangtze, and the Huai: "Issue fresh orders to chief ministers to set aside petty business and focus only on defense.

sentences.zh: 自京及荊、淮之郡，置大帥，屯勁兵。

translations.literal: From the capital to the prefectures of Jing and the Huai, appoint great commanders and station crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital through the Jing and Huai prefectures, appoint supreme commanders and station elite troops.

sentences.zh: 命沿江之守，各上措畫之方，明斥堠，設險阻，節大府之出，廣大農之入，檢察戰艦而習之，則守禦詳盡，人心安，天意回，大業昌矣。」

translations.literal: Order the governors along the river each to submit plans; make clear the outposts; establish barriers; restrain the expenditures of great prefectures and expand agricultural revenue; inspect warships and drill with them—then defense will be thorough, hearts will be at ease, heaven's intent will turn, and the great enterprise will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Require river governors to submit detailed plans, clear the signal posts, fortify choke points, curb spending from major prefectures, expand farm revenues, inspect warships and drill crews—then defenses will be sound, the people settled, heaven appeased, and the dynasty strengthened."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隆祐太后奉神主如江西，詔珏為端明殿學士、權同知三省樞密院事從行。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Longyou escorted the imperial ancestral tablets to Jiangxi. An edict made Jue Academician at the Hall of Bright Worthies and Acting Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs to accompany her.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Longyou escorted the ancestral tablets to Jiangxi, Jue was appointed Academician at the Hall of Bright Worthies and Acting Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs to accompany the tour.

sentences.zh: 時詔元祐黨籍及上書廢錮人，追復故官，錄用子孫，施行未盡者，珏悉奏行之。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered those on the Yuanyou faction register and those barred from office for submitted memorials to be restored to former posts and their sons and grandsons employed. Where implementation was incomplete, Jue memorialized to carry it all out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had ordered restoration of Yuanyou blacklist officials and those banned for memorializing, with their descendants reemployed. Where the order was incomplete, Jue memorialized to enforce it fully.

sentences.zh: 又言常安民、張克公嘗論蔡京罪，乞厚加恩。

translations.literal: He also said Chang Anmin and Zhang Kegong had once indicted Cai Jing's crimes and begged that they be richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged generous reward for Chang Anmin and Zhang Kegong, who had once indicted Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 至洪州，疏言修治巡幸道路之役，略曰：「陛下遭時艱難，躬履儉約，前冬幸淮甸，供帳弊舊，道路險狹，未嘗介意。

translations.literal: Arriving at Hongzhou, he memorialized on the labor of repairing the imperial tour route, in summary saying: "Your Majesty meets hard times and personally practices frugality. Last winter when you toured the Huai region, supplies were worn and roads narrow and dangerous—you never took it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongzhou he memorialized against repairs for the imperial route: "Your Majesty faces hard times and lives frugally. Last winter's Huai tour used worn supplies over narrow, perilous roads—you never complained.

sentences.zh: 今聞衢、信以來，除治道路，科率民丁，急如星火，廣市羊豕，備造服用，使農夫不得穫，齊民不得休，非陛下儉以避難之意也。

translations.literal: Now I hear that from Qu and Xin onward roads are being cleared, labor conscripted from the people with urgency like sparks and stars, goats and pigs bought widely, and garments prepared for manufacture, so farmers cannot harvest and common people cannot rest—this is not Your Majesty's intent to be frugal and avoid hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Now from Quzhou and Xinzhou onward I hear roads cleared, peasants conscripted at frantic pace, livestock bought in bulk, and finery prepared—farmers cannot harvest and townspeople cannot rest. This is not the frugal spirit Your Majesty showed in flight from danger.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔悉罷。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to abolish all of this entirely."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict abolish these works entirely."

sentences.zh: 金人攻吉州，分兵追太后，舟至太和縣，衛兵皆潰，珏奉太后退保虔州。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked Jizhou and sent forces in pursuit of the empress dowager. When the boats reached Taihe County the guards all fled. Jue escorted the empress dowager in withdrawal to hold Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen forces attacked Jizhou and sent columns after the empress dowager. At Taihe County the escort collapsed. Jue withdrew with the empress dowager to Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 監察御史張延壽論珏罪，珏亦上書自劾，逾嶺俟命，落職，提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zhang Yanshou indicted Jue's offense. Jue also submitted a memorial impeaching himself, crossed the mountains awaiting orders, was stripped of office, and made Administrator of Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zhang Yanshou charged Jue, who also submitted a self-impeachment, crossed the Nanling to await judgment, was dismissed, and assigned to administer Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 延壽論不已，責授秘書少監，貶衡州。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshou continued his prosecution without cease. Jue was demoted to Junior Supervisor of the Secretariat and banished to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshou pressed his case. Jue was demoted to Junior Supervisor of the Secretariat and exiled to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，許自便。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 1 he was permitted free movement.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1 he was allowed to go where he pleased.

sentences.zh: 明年，以朝散大夫分司西京。

translations.literal: The next year he served as Grand Master of Court Dispersion in the Western Capital office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he held the title Grand Master of Court Dispersion with a nominal post in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒於梧州，年五十五。

translations.literal: He died at Wuzhou at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Wuzhou, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 官其二子。

translations.literal: His two sons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his sons received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 八年，追復龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: In year 8 his Dragon Designs Academicianship was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his Dragon Designs Academicianship was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 有《吳興集》二十卷、《集議》五卷、《兩漢蒙求》十卷。

translations.literal: He had Collected Works of Wuxing in twenty juan, Collected Deliberations in five juan, and Quests through the Two Han in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Collected Works of Wuxing in twenty juan, Collected Deliberations in five juan, and Quests through the Two Han in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 胡舜陟

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi

sentences.zh: 胡舜陟，字汝明，徽州績溪人。

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi, courtesy name Ruming, was a native of Jixi in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi, styled Ruming, came from Jixi in Huizhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登大觀三年進士第，歷州縣官，為監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Daguan, served in successive prefecture and county posts, and became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned jinshi honors in Daguan 3, served in county and prefectural posts, and rose to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 奏：「御史以言為職，故自唐至本朝皆論時事，擊官邪，與殿中侍御史同。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The censor's duty is speech; therefore from Tang to this dynasty all have discussed current affairs and attacked corrupt officials, the same as Palace Aide of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "A censor's charge is to speak. From Tang through our dynasty, censors have addressed current affairs and indicted corrupt officials—no less than Palace Aides of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，大臣欲便己，遂變祖宗成憲，南臺御史始有不言事者。

translations.literal: During Chongning, great ministers wishing to convenience themselves changed the ancestral statutes, and Investigating Censors of the Southern Bureau first appeared who did not speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning, ministers bent precedent to serve themselves, and Southern Bureau investigating censors ceased remonstrating on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 多事之時，以開言路為急。

translations.literal: In a time of many crises, opening the path of speech is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In perilous times, opening the remonstrance path is urgent.

sentences.zh: 乞下本臺，增入監察御史言事之文，以復祖宗之制。」

translations.literal: I beg that this bureau be ordered to add text on Investigating Censors' right to speak on affairs, to restore the ancestral system."
translations.idiomatic: I beg an order to this bureau restoring Investigating Censors' remonstrance authority under ancestral practice."

sentences.zh: 以內艱去。

translations.literal: He departed on account of domestic mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 服闋，再為監察御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was again appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 奏：「河北金兵已遁，備禦尤不可不講。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Jurchen troops in Hebei have already withdrawn, yet preparations for defense especially cannot go undiscussed."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Though Jurchen forces have withdrawn from Hebei, border defenses must not be neglected."

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，又言：「今結成邊患，幾傾社稷，自歸明官趙良嗣始，請戮之以快天下。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong acceded he again said: "The border crisis that nearly toppled the state began with the Surrender-Illumination official Zhao Liangsi. I beg that he be executed to satisfy the realm."
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzong's accession he urged: "The border crisis that nearly destroyed the dynasty began with Surrender-Illumination official Zhao Liangsi. Execute him to satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 遂誅良嗣。

translations.literal: Liangsi was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsi was accordingly executed.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「今邊境備禦之計，兵可練，粟可積，獨將為難得，請詔內外之臣，並舉文武官才堪將帥者。」

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "For border defense, troops can be drilled and grain amassed; only generals are hard to obtain. I beg that inner and outer officials together recommend civil and military officers qualified for command."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Troops can be trained and grain stockpiled, but capable generals are scarce. Order officials throughout the empire to recommend civil and military men fit for command."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「上殿班先臺後諫，祖宗法也，今臺臣在諫臣下，乞今後臺諫同日上殿，以臺諫雜壓為先後。」

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "In the court audience formation the censorate comes before remonstrance officials—this is ancestral law. Now censorate officials stand below remonstrance officials. I beg that hereafter censors and remonstrators attend audience on the same day, precedence settled by mixed rank."
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded: "Ancestral law placed censors before remonstrators at imperial audience. Today censors rank below remonstrators. Let censors and remonstrators attend together hereafter, with mixed rank deciding precedence."

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 奏：「向者晁說之乞皇太子講《孝經》，讀《論語》，間日讀《爾雅》而廢《孟子》。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Formerly Chao Shuozhi asked that the crown prince lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, read the Analects, read the Erya on alternate days, and abandon Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: He objected: "Chao Shuozhi proposed that the crown prince study the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, read the Erya on alternate days, and drop Mencius.

sentences.zh: 夫孔子之後深知聖人之道者，孟子而已。

translations.literal: After Confucius, only Mencius deeply understood the sage's Way.
translations.idiomatic: After Confucius, Mencius alone deeply grasped the sage's Way.

sentences.zh: 願詔東宮官遵舊制，先讀《論語》，次讀《孟子》。」

translations.literal: I wish an edict would order Eastern Palace officials to follow the old system: first read the Analects, next read Mencius."
translations.idiomatic: I urge an edict ordering Eastern Palace tutors to follow precedent: first the Analects, then Mencius."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「涪陵譙定受《易》于郭雍，究極象數，逆知人事，洞曉諸葛亮八陣法，宜厚禮招之。」

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Qiao Ding of Fuling received the Changes from Guo Yong, exhaustively mastered image and number, foreknew human affairs, and thoroughly understood Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations. He should be summoned with rich courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended: "Qiao Ding of Fuling studied the Changes under Guo Yong, mastered numerology, foresaw events, and knew Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations by heart. Summon him with generous honors."

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，舜陟論宰相李綱之罪，帝不聽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, Shunzhi indicted Chancellor Li Gang's offenses. The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession Shunzhi charged Chancellor Li Gang, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 言者論其嘗事偽廷，除集英殿修撰、知廬州。

translations.literal: Critics indicted his having once served the puppet court. He was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics accused him of serving the puppet regime. He was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時淮西盜賊充斥，廬人震恐，日具舟楫為南渡計。

translations.literal: At the time bandits filled western Huai. The people of Lu were terrified and daily prepared boats and oars planning flight south.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits overran western Huai. Luzhou residents panicked and daily prepared boats for a flight south.

sentences.zh: 舜陟至，修城治戰具，人心始安。

translations.literal: When Shunzhi arrived he repaired the walls and prepared weapons, and hearts first settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzhi arrived he fortified the walls and readied arms, and the people calmed.

sentences.zh: 冀州雲騎卒孫琪聚兵為盜，號「一海蝦」，至廬，舜陟乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Sun Qi, a Cloud Cavalry soldier of Jizhou, gathered troops as a bandit and styled himself "One Sea Shrimp." Reaching Lu, Shunzhi mounted the wall to repel and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi, a Cloud Cavalry trooper from Jizhou, raised a band that he called "One Sea Shrimp." When they reached Luzhou, Shunzhi manned the walls in defense.

sentences.zh: 琪邀資糧，舜陟不與，其眾請以粟遺之，舜陟曰：「吾非有所愛，顧賊心無厭，與之則示弱，彼無能為也。」

translations.literal: Qi demanded provisions. Shunzhi would not give them. His men asked to send grain as a gift. Shunzhi said: "It is not that I begrudge anything; I only consider that bandits' hearts know no satisfaction. Giving would show weakness, and they can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Qi demanded supplies. Shunzhi refused. When his men urged sending grain, he said: "It is not stinginess—these bandits are insatiable. To yield would show weakness, and they cannot prevail anyway."

sentences.zh: 乃時出兵擊其抄掠者，琪宵遁，舜陟伏兵邀擊，得其輜重而歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent troops at intervals to strike their raiders. Qi fled by night. Shunzhi's ambush intercepted him and seized his baggage train in returning.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent out troops to harry the raiders. Qi fled by night. Shunzhi's ambush cut him off and captured his baggage train.

sentences.zh: 濟南僧劉文舜聚黨萬餘，保舒州投子山縱剽，舜陟遣介使招降之。

translations.literal: The monk Liu Wenshun of Jinan gathered a party of more than ten thousand, held Mount Touzi in Shuzhou, and roved in plunder. Shunzhi sent an envoy to summon surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinan monk Liu Wenshun rallied more than ten thousand men, seized Mount Touzi in Shuzhou, and raided freely. Shunzhi sent envoys to accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 時丁進、李勝合兵為盜蘄、壽間，舜陟遣文舜破之。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Jin and Li Sheng combined forces as bandits between Qi and Shou. Shunzhi sent Wenshun to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Jin and Li Sheng had joined forces as bandits between Qizhou and Shouzhou. Shunzhi dispatched Wenshun to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 張遇自濠州奄至梁縣，舜陟使毀竹里橋，伏兵河西，伺其半渡擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu suddenly arrived at Liang County from Haozhou. Shunzhi had Zhuli Bridge destroyed, placed ambush west of the river, waited until they were half across, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu swept from Haozhou upon Liang County. Shunzhi had Zhuli Bridge destroyed, hid troops west of the river, and struck as the enemy was mid-crossing.

sentences.zh: 又請以身守江北，以護行宮。

translations.literal: He again asked to guard the north of the river with his own person to protect the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also volunteered to hold the north bank personally to shield the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，擢徽猷閣待制，充淮西制置使。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his words, promoted him to Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning, and made him Huai West Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed, the emperor promoted him to Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning and appointed him Huai West Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 范瓊自壽春渡淮，貽書責贍軍錢帛，舜陟諭以逆順，瓊乃去。

translations.literal: Fan Qiong crossed the Huai from Shouchun and sent a letter demanding army pay in coin and cloth. Shunzhi admonished him on loyalty and rebellion, and Qiong then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong crossed the Huai from Shouchun and demanded army pay by letter. Shunzhi lectured him on loyalty versus rebellion, and Fan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自軍興後，淮西八郡，群盜攻蹂無全城，舜陟守廬二年，按堵如故，以徽猷閣待制知建康府，充沿江都制置使。

translations.literal: Since the army was raised, in the eight Huai West prefectures bandits attacked and ravaged with not one whole city. Shunzhi held Lu for two years and peace remained as before. He was made Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning and prefect of Jiankang, and River Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began, bandits had ravaged all eight Huai West prefectures without leaving a city intact. Shunzhi held Luzhou for two years in undisturbed order. He was then made Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning, prefect of Jiankang, and overall River Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改知臨安府，復為徽猷閣待制，充京畿數路宣撫使。

translations.literal: After a year he was changed to prefect of Lin'an, again made Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning, and Capital Region Pacification Commissioner for several circuits.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became prefect of Lin'an, was reappointed Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning, and Pacification Commissioner for several Capital Region circuits.

sentences.zh: 尋罷，遷廬、壽鎮撫使，改淮西安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon dismissed, he was transferred to Commander of Lu and Shou, then changed to Huai West Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon dismissed, he was made Commander of Luzhou and Shouzhou, then Huai West Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至廬州，潰兵王全與其徒來降，舜陟散財發粟，流民漸歸。

translations.literal: Arriving at Luzhou, routed soldier Wang Quan and his followers came to surrender. Shunzhi distributed wealth and issued grain, and displaced people gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou, routed troops under Wang Quan surrendered. Shunzhi distributed funds and grain, and refugees gradually returned.

sentences.zh: 改知靜江府，詔措置市戰馬。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Jingjiang. An edict ordered him to arrange purchase of war horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned prefect of Jingjiang with orders to procure war horses.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞常同奏舜陟兇暴傾險，罷之。

translations.literal: Investigation Commissioner Chang Tong memorialized that Shunzhi was violent, cruel, and devious, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation Commissioner Chang Tong charged Shunzhi with brutality and treachery, and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 後十八年，復為廣西經略。

translations.literal: Eighteen years later he was again made Guangxi Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years later he was restored as Guangxi Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以知邕州俞儋有贓，為運副呂源所按，事連舜陟，提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Because Yongzhou prefect Yu Dan had embezzled and was prosecuted by Transport Vice Commissioner Lü Yuan, the matter implicated Shunzhi, and he was made Administrator of Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzhou prefect Yu Dan was prosecuted for corruption by Transport Vice Commissioner Lü Yuan, the case implicated Shunzhi, who was reassigned to administer Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 先是，舜陟與源有隙，舜陟因討郴賊，劾源沮軍事，源以書抵秦檜，訟舜陟受金盜馬，非訕朝政。

translations.literal: Previously Shunzhi and Yuan had a rift. Shunzhi, while suppressing bandits in Chen, impeached Yuan for obstructing military affairs. Yuan wrote to Qin Hui accusing Shunzhi of taking bribes and stealing horses—not satirizing court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi and Yuan had long been at odds. While campaigning against Chen bandits, Shunzhi impeached Yuan for hindering operations. Yuan wrote Qin Hui accusing Shunzhi of bribery and horse theft—charges short of sedition.

sentences.zh: 檜素惡舜陟，入其說，奏遣大理寺官袁柟、燕仰之往推劾，居兩旬，辭不服，死獄中。

translations.literal: Hui had always hated Shunzhi and adopted his account. He memorialized to send Ministry of Justice officials Yuan Nan and Yan Yangzhi to investigate. After twenty days Shunzhi would not confess and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had long disliked Shunzhi and accepted Yuan's story. He dispatched Ministry of Justice investigators Yuan Nan and Yan Yangzhi. After twenty days Shunzhi would not confess and died in custody.

sentences.zh: 舜陟有惠愛，邦人聞其死，為之哭。

translations.literal: Shunzhi had benevolence and affection. When the people of the state heard of his death they wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi had been beloved by the people. When word of his death spread, they wept.

sentences.zh: 妻江氏訴於朝，詔通判德慶府洪元英究實。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Jiang, appealed to the court. An edict ordered Hong Yuanying, prefectural vice commissioner of Deqing, to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Jiang appealed to court. Hong Yuanying, vice prefect of Deqing, was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 元英言：「舜陟受金盜馬，事涉曖昧，其得人心，雖古循吏無以過。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "Shunzhi's taking bribes and stealing horses was ambiguous in the facts, yet in winning hearts even ancient model officials could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying reported: "The bribery and horse-theft charges were unclear, yet in winning popular loyalty even ancient model officials scarcely surpassed him."

sentences.zh: 帝謂檜曰：「舜陟從官，又罪不至死，勘官不可不懲。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Hui: "Shunzhi was a follower official, and moreover the offense did not merit death. The investigating officials cannot go unpunished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Hui: "Shunzhi was a court follower, and the charge did not warrant death. The investigators must be punished."

sentences.zh: 遂送柟、仰之吏部。

translations.literal: Yuan Nan and Yangzhi were thereupon sent to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Nan and Yangzhi were referred to the Ministry of Personnel for discipline.

sentences.zh: 沈晦，字元用，錢塘人，翰林學士沈遘孫。

translations.literal: Shen Hui, courtesy name Yuanyong, was a native of Qiantang and grandson of Hanlin Academician Shen Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui, styled Yuanyong, came from Qiantang and was grandson of Hanlin Academician Shen Kui.

sentences.zh: 宣和間進士廷對第一，除校書郎，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: During Xuanhe he placed first in the jinshi palace examination, was made Collator, and was transferred to Assistant Editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe era he placed first in the jinshi palace debate, became Collator, and rose to Assistant Editor.

sentences.zh: 金人攻汴京，借給事中從肅王樞出質斡離不軍。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Bianjing he was temporarily made Supervising Censor and followed Prince Su in going out as hostage to Wanyan Zonghan's army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged Bianjing he served temporarily as Supervising Censor and accompanied Prince Su as hostage to Wanyan Zonghan's camp.

sentences.zh: 金人再攻也，與之俱南。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked again he went south with them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens attacked again he was marched south with the captives.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，邦昌偽立，請金人歸馮澥等，晦因得還，真為給事中。

translations.literal: When the capital fell and Zhang Bangchang was falsely enthroned, he requested the Jurchens return Feng Xi and others. Hui thus obtained return and was truly made Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell and Zhang Bangchang's puppet regime was installed, he secured the Jurchens' release of Feng Xi and others and returned home, receiving a formal appointment as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，言者論晦雖使金艱苦，而封駁之職不可以賞勞，除集英殿修撰、知信州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded, critics argued that though Hui had endured hardship as envoy to the Jin, the sealing-and-return duty could not reward labor. He was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession critics argued that embassy hardship did not qualify Hui for the sealing-and-return post. He was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝如揚州，將召為中書舍人，侍御史張守論晦為布衣時事，帝曰：「頃在金營見其慷慨，士人細行，豈足為終身累邪？」

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Yangzhou he was about to summon Hui as Palace Secretariat Drafter. Attending Censor Zhang Shou indicted Hui's conduct as a commoner. The emperor said: "Recently in the Jurchen camp I saw him bold and generous. Are a gentleman's minor acts enough to burden him for life?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou the emperor planned to recall Hui as Palace Secretariat Drafter. Attending Censor Zhang Shou revived rumors of Hui's youth. The emperor replied: "I saw his courage in the Jurchen camp. Must petty youthful conduct haunt a man forever?"

sentences.zh: 不果召。

translations.literal: The summoning was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment did not proceed.

sentences.zh: 知明州，移處州。

translations.literal: He governed Mingzhou and was transferred to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Mingzhou, then Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝如會稽，移守婺州。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Kuaiji he was transferred to guard Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Kuaiji he was reassigned prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊成皋入寇，晦用教授孫邦策，率民兵數百出城與戰，大敗，晦欲斬邦，已而釋之。

translations.literal: Bandit Chenggao invaded. Hui followed Instructor Sun Bang's plan, led several hundred militia out of the city to fight, and suffered great defeat. Hui wished to execute Bang but afterward released him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Chenggao invaded. Following Instructor Sun Bang's advice, Hui led several hundred militiamen out to fight and was routed. He nearly executed Bang but relented.

sentences.zh: 時浙東防遏使傅崧卿在城中，單騎往說皋，皋遂降。

translations.literal: At the time Zhedong Defense Commissioner Fu Songqing was in the city. He went alone on horseback to persuade Chenggao, and Chenggao then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhedong Defense Commissioner Fu Songqing was in the city. He rode out alone, persuaded Chenggao, and secured his surrender.

sentences.zh: 進徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning.

sentences.zh: 以言者論晦妄用便宜指揮行事，降集英殿修撰、提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Because critics indicted Hui for arbitrarily exercising discretionary command, he was demoted to Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and Administrator of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged Hui with abusing discretionary authority. He was demoted to Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and assigned to administer Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 尋復徽猷閣待制、知宣州，移知建康府。

translations.literal: Soon restored as Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning and prefect of Xuanzhou, he was transferred to prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as Awaiting Drafting at the Hall of Majestic Planning at Xuanzhou, he was transferred to prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 甫逾月，以御史常同論罷。

translations.literal: Just over a month later he was dismissed on Attending Censor Chang Tong's indictment.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later Attending Censor Chang Tong's charges removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，起知鎮江府、兩浙西路安撫使，過行在面對，言：「藩帥之兵可用。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 4 he was raised to prefect of Zhenjiang and Pacification Commissioner of western Two Zhe circuits. Passing the traveling capital he had face audience and said: "The forces of frontier commanders can be used.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 4 he was recalled as prefect of Zhenjiang and Pacification Commissioner of western Two Zhe. At the mobile court he argued: "Frontier commanders' troops can be put to use.

sentences.zh: 今沿江千餘里，若令鎮江、建康、太平、池、鄂五郡各有兵一二萬，以本郡財賦易官田給之，敵至，五郡以舟師守江，步兵守隘，彼難自渡。

translations.literal: Today along more than a thousand li of the river, if Zhenjiang, Jiankang, Taiping, Chi, and E prefectures each held ten or twenty thousand troops, paying them from local revenues in exchange for official fields, when the enemy comes the five prefectures would use river fleets to guard the river and infantry to hold passes—they would find it hard to cross on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Along the thousand-li Yangtze line, let Zhenjiang, Jiankang, Taiping, Chizhou, and Ezhou each maintain ten to twenty thousand men, paid from local revenues via purchase of official fields. When enemies come, the five prefectures can block the river with fleets and hold the passes with infantry—the foe cannot cross unaided.

sentences.zh: 假使參渡，五郡合擊，敵雖善戰，不能一日破諸城也。

translations.literal: Even if they crossed in part, the five prefectures would strike together; though the enemy excels in warfare, they could not break all the cities in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Even partial crossings could be met by a joint counterstrike from all five prefectures. However skilled the enemy, they could not take every city in a day.

sentences.zh: 若圍五郡，則兵分勢弱，或以偏師綴我大軍南侵，則五郡尾而邀之，敵安敢遠去。

translations.literal: If they besieged the five prefectures their forces would be divided and weakened. Or if a detached column pinioned our main army in a southward invasion, the five prefectures would follow and intercept from the rear—how would the enemy dare go far?
translations.idiomatic: Besieging all five would spread their forces thin. If a detachment pinned our main army during a southern drive, the five prefectures could harry their rear—enemies would not dare advance far.

sentences.zh: 此制稍定，三年後移江北，糧餉、器械悉自隨。」

translations.literal: Once this system is somewhat settled, after three years move to the north of the river, provisions and weapons all following of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Once this system is established, after three years transfer north of the river with supplies and arms self-sufficient."

sentences.zh: 又自乞分兵二千及召募敢戰士三千，參用昭義步兵法，期年後，京口便成強藩。

translations.literal: He also personally requested two thousand troops divided to him and three thousand bold fighters recruited, adopting the Zhaoyi infantry method; within a year Jingkou would become a strong frontier prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for two thousand assigned troops and three thousand recruits trained in the Zhaoyi infantry method, promising that within a year Jingkou would become a strong defensive prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時方以韓世忠屯軍鎮江，不果用。

translations.literal: At the time Han Shizhong's army was already stationed at Zhenjiang, and his plan was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong already held Zhenjiang with his army, so the plan was rejected.

sentences.zh: 劉麟入寇，世忠拒於揚州，晦乞促張俊兵為世忠援。

translations.literal: Liu Lin invaded. Shizhong resisted at Yangzhou. Hui begged that Zhang Jun's troops be urged as relief for Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Lin invaded, Shizhong fought at Yangzhou. Hui urged dispatch of Zhang Jun's forces to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎稱晦議論激昂，帝曰：「晦誠可嘉，然朕知其人言甚壯，膽志頗怯，更觀臨事，能副所言與否？」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding praised Hui's discourse as impassioned. The emperor said: "Hui is indeed admirable, yet I know the man—his words are very bold but his courage and resolve rather timid. Watch further whether in the event he can match what he says."
