translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding praised Hui's fervor. The emperor replied: "Hui deserves credit, but I know him—bold in speech, timid in spirit. We shall see whether action matches words."

sentences.zh: 然晦不為世忠所樂，尋提舉臨安府洞霄宮，起為廣西經略兼知靜江府。

translations.literal: Yet Hui was not favored by Shizhong. Soon he was made Administrator of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an, then raised as Guangxi Military Commissioner and concurrently prefect of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong disliked Hui nonetheless. Hui was soon assigned to Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an, then recalled as Guangxi Military Commissioner and prefect of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 先是，南州蠻酋莫公晟歸朝，歲久，用為本路鈐轄羈縻之，後遁去，旁結諸峒蠻，歲出為邊患。

translations.literal: Previously the Man chieftain Mo Gongsheng of the southern prefectures submitted to the court. After many years he was used as Circuit Controller of his circuit to keep him restrained by attachment. Later he fled, allied with neighboring cave Man, and each year raided as a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the southern Man chieftain Mo Gongsheng had submitted to the court. After long service as a nominal circuit controller he fled, rallied neighboring cave tribes, and annually raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 晦選老將羅統戍邊，招誘諸酋，喻以威信，皆詣府請降，晦犒遺之，結誓而去。

translations.literal: Hui selected veteran general Luo Tong to garrison the border, enticed the various chieftains, instructed them with authority and trust, and all came to the prefecture to request surrender. Hui rewarded and sent them off, and they departed having sworn oaths.
translations.idiomatic: Hui assigned veteran general Luo Tong to guard the frontier, won over the chieftains with pledges of authority and trust, and all came to the prefectural seat to submit. He rewarded them and sent them away bound by oath.

sentences.zh: 自是公晟孤立，不復犯邊。

translations.literal: From this Gongsheng stood alone, and no longer violated the border.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Gongsheng was isolated and ceased raiding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 晦在郡，歲買馬三千匹，繼者皆不能及。

translations.literal: While Hui was in the prefecture, each year he purchased three thousand horses; successors all could not match this.
translations.idiomatic: During Hui's tenure the prefecture annually procured three thousand horses—a figure none of his successors could match.

sentences.zh: 進徽猷閣直學士，召赴行在，除知衢州，改潭州，提舉太平興國宮，卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning, summoned to the mobile court, appointed prefect of Quzhou, changed to Tanzhou, made Administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning, he was summoned to the mobile court, served as prefect of Quzhou and then Tanzhou, administered the Taiping Xingguo Palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 晦膽氣過人，不能盡循法度，貧時尤甚，故累致人言。

translations.literal: Hui's boldness and spirit surpassed others; he could not fully follow statutes and regulations. When poor it was especially so, hence he repeatedly drew people's talk.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was bolder than most and often skirted the law—especially when he was poor—drawing repeated criticism.

sentences.zh: 然其當官才具，亦不可掩云。

translations.literal: Yet his talent for holding office also could not be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his competence in office could not be denied.

sentences.zh: 劉一止

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi

sentences.zh: 劉一止，字行簡，湖州歸安人。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi, courtesy name Xingjian, was a native of Gui'an in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi, styled Xingjian, came from Gui'an in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲能屬文，試太學，有司欲舉八行，一止曰：「行者士之常。」

translations.literal: At seven sui he could compose prose. Entering the Imperial College, the authorities wished to recommend him for the Eight Virtues. Yizhi said: "Conduct is the scholar's constant."
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already write essays. When tested at the Imperial College, officials sought to nominate him for the Eight Virtues. Yizhi replied: "Virtuous conduct is what every scholar should possess."

sentences.zh: 不就。

translations.literal: He did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the honor.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為越州教授。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became instructor at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination, he was appointed instructor at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 參知政事李邴薦為詳定一司敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Li Bing recommended him as revising officer of the Commission for Revising Statutes of a Single Office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Li Bing recommended him as a revising officer on the Commission for Revising Statutes of a Single Office.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，召試館職，其略曰：「事不克濟者，患在不為，不患其難，聖人不畏多難，以因難而圖事耳。

translations.literal: In the early Shaoxing era he was summoned to test for an academy post. The gist of his essay said: "Where affairs fail to succeed, the worry lies in not acting—not in their difficulty. The sage does not fear many difficulties; he uses difficulty to accomplish affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing reign he was called to compete for an academy appointment. His essay argued: "What defeats great undertakings is inaction, not difficulty. The sage does not dread hardship; he turns hardship to purpose.

sentences.zh: 如其不為，俟天命自回，人事自正，敵國自屈，盜賊自平，有是哉？」

translations.literal: If one does not act, waiting for Heaven's mandate to turn of itself, human affairs to right themselves, enemy states to submit of themselves, and bandits to pacify themselves—is there such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Without action, can one wait for Heaven to reverse itself, affairs to right themselves, enemies to submit, and bandits to disperse of their own accord?"

sentences.zh: 高宗稱善，且諭近臣以所言剴切知治道，欲驟用，執政不樂，除秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Gaozong praised it and moreover instructed close ministers that his words were incisive and showed knowledge of governance; he wished to employ him abruptly, but the chief ministers were displeased, and he was appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong approved and told his inner circle that the essay showed sharp insight into governance; he wished to promote Yizhi at once, but the chief ministers resisted, and Yizhi was made collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 考兩浙類試，以科舉方變，欲得通時務者，同列皆患無其人，一止出一卷曰：「是宜為首。」

translations.literal: Examining the classified examination of the Two Zhes, as the civil-service system was changing they wished to obtain men versed in current affairs. Colleagues all worried there was no such person. Yizhi produced one scroll and said: "This one should rank first."
translations.idiomatic: During the Two Zhes classified examination, with the civil-service system in flux the examiners sought candidates versed in current affairs. Colleagues despaired of finding any. Yizhi produced one paper and said: "This should take first place."

sentences.zh: 啟號乃張九成也，眾皆厭服。

translations.literal: When the name was opened it was Zhang Jiucheng; all were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The name proved to be Zhang Jiucheng, and all conceded.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏謂：「天下之治，眾君子成之而不足，一小人敗之而有餘，君子雖眾道則孤，小人雖寡勢易蔓，不加察，則小人伺隙而入以敗政矣。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "The governance of the realm—many gentlemen may build it yet it is insufficient; one petty man may ruin it and have to spare. Though gentlemen are many, the Way is solitary; though petty men are few, their influence spreads easily. Without careful scrutiny, petty men watch for openings and enter to ruin government."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Good government requires many worthy men yet can still fail; one base man can destroy it with ease. Worthies may be numerous, but the Way stands alone; villains may be few, yet their power spreads. Without vigilance, petty men slip through the cracks and wreck the state."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下憫宿蠹未除，頹綱未振，民困財竭，故置司講究，然未聞有所施行，得無有以疑似之說欺陛下，曰 『如此，將失人心』。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty pities that old abuses are not removed, collapsed norms are not restored, the people are distressed and revenues exhausted, and therefore established offices to investigate—yet I have not heard of anything implemented. Might there not be those who deceive Your Majesty with doubtful talk, saying, 'If we do this, we will lose the people's hearts'?
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Your Majesty, grieving that old abuses persist and institutions lie in ruins while the people suffer and coffers run dry, established offices to study reform—yet nothing has been enacted. Are sycophants not deceiving you with warnings that reform will 'lose the people's hearts'?

sentences.zh: 夫所謂失人心者，必刑政之苛，賦役之多，好惡之不公，賞罰之不明；

translations.literal: What is called losing the people's hearts must be harsh punishments and government, heavy taxes and corvée, partial likes and dislikes, unclear rewards and punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Losing the people's hearts means cruel law, crushing levies, biased favor, and muddled rewards and punishments—

sentences.zh: 若皆無是，則所失者小人之心耳，何病焉。」

translations.literal: if none of these exist, then what is lost is only petty men's hearts—what harm is there?"
translations.idiomatic: if none of these apply, only petty men lose heart. What harm is that?"

sentences.zh: 時庶事草創，有司以吏所省記為法，吏並緣為姦，一止曰：「法令具在，吏猶得舞文，矧一切聽其省記，所欲與則陳與例，欲奪則陳奪例，與奪在其牙頰，患可勝言哉！

translations.literal: At the time myriad affairs were newly founded; offices took clerks' abbreviated notes as law, and clerks all used them as pretexts for wrongdoing. Yizhi said: "Statutes are fully in place, yet clerks still twist the law—how much more if everything follows their abbreviated notes! What they wish to grant they cite a granting precedent; what they wish to seize they cite a seizing precedent. Grant and seize lie on their lips—the harm is beyond words!
translations.idiomatic: With the state still rebuilding, departments treated clerks' shorthand notes as law, inviting abuse. Yizhi warned: "Full statutes already allow clerks to twist the law—how much worse if everything rests on their private notes! To grant a favor they cite one precedent; to deny one they cite another. Power sits on their tongues—the mischief is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 請以省記之文刊定頒行，庶幾絕姦吏弄法受賕之弊。」

translations.literal: I ask that the text of the abbreviated notes be edited, printed, and promulgated, so as to cut off the abuse of corrupt clerks manipulating law and taking bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Publish the official text of those notes after editorial review, to end corrupt clerks' manipulation of law and acceptance of bribes."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 逾年而書成。

translations.literal: After more than a year the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the compilation was finished.

sentences.zh: 秦檜請置修政局，一止言：「宣王內修政事，修其外攘之政而已。

translations.literal: Qin Hui requested establishment of a Bureau for Administrative Reform. Yizhi said: "King Xuan inwardly cultivated government affairs—he cultivated the policies for outward defense, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui proposed a Bureau for Administrative Reform, Yizhi objected: "King Xuan of Zhou reformed government at home to strengthen defense abroad—that was all.

sentences.zh: 今之所修，特簿書獄訟，官吏遷降，土木營建之務，未見所當急也。」

translations.literal: What is now being reformed is only bookkeeping, lawsuits, officials' promotions and demotions, and construction works—I do not see what should be urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Today's 'reform' covers paperwork, litigation, personnel moves, and construction—hardly the urgent matters."

sentences.zh: 又謂：「人才進用太遽，仕者或不由銓選，朝士入而不出，外官雖有異能，不見召用，非軍事而起復，皆幸門不塞之故。

translations.literal: He also said: "Talent is promoted too hastily. Some officeholders bypass the Board of Appointments; court officials enter and do not leave; outside officials though possessing special ability are not summoned; those returning to service without military need—all because the gate of favoritism is not blocked.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned: "Appointments come too fast. Some bypass the Board of Appointments; court officials enter and never leave; able local officials go uncalled; non-military recall flourishes—all because favoritism runs unchecked.

sentences.zh: 請選近臣曉財利者，仿劉晏法，瀕江置司以制國用，鄉村置義倉以備水旱，增重監司之選。」

translations.literal: I ask that close ministers versed in finance be selected, following Liu Yan's method, to establish offices along the river to control state expenditures; establish charity granaries in villages and hamlets to prepare for flood and drought; and increase the weight of circuit-intendant selection."
translations.idiomatic: Select close ministers skilled in finance, adopt Liu Yan's methods, establish riverine offices to manage state revenue, set up charity granaries in the countryside against flood and drought, and raise standards for circuit-intendant appointments."

sentences.zh: 後多採用其言。

translations.literal: Later many of his words were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his proposals were later adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He was made diarist.

sentences.zh: 奏事，帝迎語曰：「朕親擢也，繇六察遷二史，祖宗時有幾？」

translations.literal: Presenting business, the emperor greeted him and said: "I personally promoted you—from the Six Investigators to the Two Diarists; in the times of the ancestors how many were there?"
translations.idiomatic: When he reported to the throne, the emperor greeted him: "I promoted you myself—from investigating censor to diarist. How often did our forebears do that?"

sentences.zh: 一止謝：「先朝惟張澂、李棁耳。」

translations.literal: Yizhi thanked him: "In the previous reign only Zhang Cheng and Li Zong."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi replied: "Under the previous emperor, only Zhang Cheng and Li Zong."

sentences.zh: 因極陳堂吏宦官之蠹，執政植私黨，無憂國心。

translations.literal: He then fully set forth the harm of bureau clerks and eunuchs, that the chief ministers planted private factions and had no mind to worry for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He then denounced bureau clerks and eunuchs, charging that chief ministers built private factions and cared nothing for the realm.

sentences.zh: 翌日罷，主管台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: The next day he was dismissed and made Administrator of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was dismissed to administer the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 召為祠部郎、知袁州，改浙東路提點刑獄，為秘書少監，復除起居郎，擢中書舍人兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director in the Ministry of Rites and prefect of Yuanzhou, changed to judicial intendant of the Eastern Zhe Circuit, made vice director of the Secretariat, again appointed diarist, and promoted to Secretariat drafter and concurrently expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as director in the Ministry of Rites and prefect of Yuanzhou, he became judicial intendant of Eastern Zhe, vice director of the Secretariat, diarist again, then Secretariat drafter and court expositor.

sentences.zh: 莫將賜出身除起居郎，一止奏：「將以上書助和議，驟自太府丞綴從班，前此未有，臣乃與將同命，願並臣罷之。」

translations.literal: Mo Jiang was granted initial appointment and appointed diarist. Yizhi memorialized: "Jiang, for submitting a memorial supporting the peace talks, abruptly rose from vice director of the Palace Storehouse to join the close retinue—unprecedented before. I am appointed together with Jiang; I ask that I be dismissed along with him."
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Jiang received direct appointment as diarist for memorializing in favor of peace talks—leaping from vice director of the Palace Storehouse into the inner court, an unprecedented rise—Yizhi protested: "I share this appointment with Jiang; dismiss us both."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising drafter.

sentences.zh: 徐偉達者，嘗事張邦昌為郎，得知池州，一止言：「偉達既仕偽廷，今付以郡，無以示天下。」

translations.literal: Xu Weida had once served Zhang Bangchang as a court gentleman and was appointed prefect of Chizhou. Yizhi said: "Weida already served the puppet court; to entrust him with a prefecture gives no sign to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Weida had served Zhang Bangchang's puppet regime as a court gentleman and was now made prefect of Chizhou. Yizhi objected: "Having served a usurper, he should not govern a commandery—it sets a ruinous example."

sentences.zh: 孟忠厚乞試郡，一止言：「后族業文如忠厚雖可為郡，他日有援例者，何以卻之？

translations.literal: Meng Zhonghou begged trial appointment to a prefecture. Yizhi said: "A consort clansman and literary man like Zhonghou may indeed govern a prefecture, but if someone later cites precedent, how will you refuse?
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhonghou, a consort clansman, sought a trial prefectural appointment. Yizhi argued: "Men of letters among the empress's kin may serve, but what precedent will you cite when others follow?

sentences.zh: {」汪伯彥知宣州入覲，詔以元帥府舊人，特依見任執政給奉，一止言：「伯彥誤國之罪，天下共知，以郡守而例執政，殆與異時非待制而視待制，非兩府而視兩府者類矣。」

translations.literal: " Wang Boyan, prefect of Xuanzhou, came to audience. An edict, because he was an old member of the Marshal's Office, specially granted salary according to an incumbent chief minister. Yizhi said: "Boyan's crime of misleading the state is known to all. For a prefect to receive chief-minister salary is much like the old cases of treating a non-vice-director as a vice-director, or a non-councillor as a councillor."
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Boyan, prefect of Xuanzhou, came to court. Because he had served in the Marshal's Office, an edict granted him a chief minister's stipend. Yizhi protested: "Boyan's betrayal is notorious. Giving a prefect a councillor's pay repeats the old abuse of inflating ranks without title."

sentences.zh: 帝皆為罷之，於凡貴近之請，雖小事亦論執不置。

translations.literal: The emperor set aside all of them. In every request from the noble and close, though a small matter, he argued and held firm without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected all three nominations. On every favor sought by the powerful—even trifles—Yizhi argued and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞廖剛謂其僚曰：「臺當有言者，皆為劉君先矣。」

translations.literal: Investigating censor-in-chief Liao Gang said to his colleagues: "The Censorate ought to speak—but Liu Jun has spoken ahead on everything."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor-in-chief Liao Gang told his staff: "We censors should speak out—but Liu Yizhi always beats us to it."

sentences.zh: 居瑣闥百餘日，繳奏不已，用事者始忌，奏一止同周葵薦呂廣問，迎合李光，罷，提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the inner gates more than a hundred days, submitting rebuttals without cease. Those in power began to resent him and memorialized that Yizhi, together with Zhou Kui, had recommended Lü Guangwen, currying favor with Li Guang. He was dismissed and made Administrator of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days in the inner court, his rebuttals never ceased. The powerful turned against him, accusing him of joining Zhou Kui in recommending Lü Guangwen to court Li Guang. He was dismissed to administer the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director of the Hall of Dispersed Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Hall of Dispersed Literature.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞何若奏：「一止朋附光，偃蹇慢上。」

translations.literal: Investigating censor-in-chief He Ruo memorialized: "Yizhi cliques with Guang, is arrogant and disrespectful to the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor-in-chief He Ruo charged that Yizhi "factions with Li Guang and treats the throne with arrogance."

sentences.zh: 落職，罷祠。

translations.literal: His office was stripped and his abbey appointment revoked.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank and lost his abbey post.

sentences.zh: 後八年，請老，復職，致仕。

translations.literal: After eight years he requested old age leave, was restored to office, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later he requested retirement, was restored to rank, and retired.

sentences.zh: 秦檜死，召至國門，以病不能拜，力辭，進直學士，致仕。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died he was summoned to the capital gate; because of illness he could not bow and forcefully declined, was advanced to academician and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui's death he was summoned to the capital but, too ill to bow, firmly declined; he was granted academician rank and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十三。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 一止沖淡寡欲，嘗誨其子曰：「吾平生通塞，聽于自然，唯機械不生，故方寸自有樂地。」

translations.literal: Yizhi was mild and of few desires. He once admonished his sons: "Through my life advance and obstruction I have listened to nature; only because artifice does not arise does my breast have its own place of joy."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was serene and ascetic. He told his sons: "Advancement and setback I leave to fate; because I harbor no scheming, my heart knows its own peace."

sentences.zh: 博學無不通，為文不事纖刻，制誥坦明有體，書詔一日數十輒辦，嘗言：「訓誥者，賞善罰惡詞也，豈過情溢美、怒鄰罵坐之為哉。」

translations.literal: He was broadly learned without anything not mastered. In writing he did not pursue fine carving. His edicts were plain and had structure. Several dozen edicts and proclamations in a day he finished at once. He once said: "Instruction and edict are words to reward good and punish evil—how could they be excessive praise or vent anger at neighbors and curse the innocent?
translations.idiomatic: Learned in all fields, he wrote without ornament. His edicts were lucid and well-formed; he could draft dozens in a day. "Imperial words reward virtue and punish vice," he said—"they must not flatter beyond merit or curse the innocent in rage."

sentences.zh: 其草顏魯公孫特命官制甚偉，帝歎賞，為手書之。

translations.literal: His draft for the specially appointed office for Yan Lugong's grandson was very grand; the emperor sighed in admiration and copied it in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: His draft appointing a grandson of Yan Zhenqing to special office was so fine the emperor admired it and copied it by hand.

sentences.zh: 詩自成家，呂本中、陳與義讀之曰：「語不自人間來也。」

translations.literal: His poetry formed its own school. Lü Benzhong and Chen Yuyi, reading it, said: "These words do not come from the human world."
translations.idiomatic: His poetry stood apart. Lü Benzhong and Chen Yuyi read it and marveled: "Language like this does not belong to this world."

sentences.zh: 有類稿五十卷。

translations.literal: He had fifty juan of collected drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He left fifty juan of collected drafts.

sentences.zh: 子巒、嶅，從弟寧止。

translations.literal: His sons Luan and Yao; his cousin Ningzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Luan and Yao; his cousin was Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 從弟 寧止

translations.literal: Cousin Ningzhi
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Ningzhi

sentences.zh: 寧止，字無虞，登宣和進士甲科，除太學錄、校書郎。

translations.literal: Ningzhi, courtesy name Wuyu, passed the Xuanhe jinshi examination in the first class, and was appointed recorder of the Imperial College and collator.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi, styled Wuyu, passed the Xuanhe jinshi in the top class and became Imperial College recorder and collator.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，為浙西安撫大使司參議，改兩浙轉運判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era he was staff officer of the Pacification Commission of Western Zhe, and was changed to transport judge of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he served on the Western Zhe Pacification staff, then as transport judge of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 苗傅、劉正彥之變，寧止自毗陵馳詣京口、金陵，見呂頤浩、劉光世，勉以忠義，退而具軍須以佐勤王。

translations.literal: In the mutiny of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan, Ningzhi raced from Piling to Jingkou and Jinling, saw Lü Yihao and Liu Guangshi, exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness, withdrew and fully prepared military supplies to aid the loyalist armies.
translations.idiomatic: During the mutiny of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan, Ningzhi rode from Piling to Jingkou and Jinling, urged Lü Yihao and Liu Guangshi to loyalty, then gathered supplies for the loyalist cause.

sentences.zh: 除左司郎官，辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed director in the Left Department and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed director in the Left Department, he declined.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，除右司郎官、給事中。

translations.literal: When the emperor resumed the throne he was appointed director in the Right Department and supervising drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's restoration he became director in the Right Department and supervising drafter.

sentences.zh: 梁揚祖為發運使，寧止再疏論駁。

translations.literal: Liang Yangzu was made transport commissioner; Ningzhi twice submitted memorials rebutting it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Yangzu was made transport commissioner, Ningzhi memorialized twice in opposition.

sentences.zh: 以添差江、淮、荊湖制置發運副使扈從隆祐太后幸江西，尋為兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: As supernumerary vice commissioner of the Jiang-Huai-Jing-Hu Pacification Transport Commission he escorted Empress Dowager Longyou on her journey to Jiangxi, and soon became vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: As supernumerary vice transport commissioner he escorted Empress Dowager Longyou to Jiangxi, then served as vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 錄勤王功，直龍圖閣，進秘閣修撰，主管崇道觀，提點江淮等路坑冶鑄錢，知鎮江府兼沿江安撫，進右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: Recording merit in aiding the loyalist armies, he was made Direct Aide of the Dragon Diagram Hall, advanced to compiler of the Secret Archive, Administrator of the Chongdao Abbey, intendant of mining and coinage along the Jiang-Huai routes, prefect of Zhenjiang and concurrently riverine pacification commissioner, and advanced to compiler of the Hall of Right Culture.
translations.idiomatic: For loyalist service he was made Direct Aide of the Dragon Diagram Hall, Secret Archive compiler, administrator of the Chongdao Abbey, intendant of mining and coinage on the Jiang-Huai routes, prefect of Zhenjiang and riverine pacification commissioner, then compiler of the Hall of Right Culture.

sentences.zh: 寧止言：「京口控扼大江，為浙西門戶，請分常州、江陰軍及昆山、常熟二縣隸本司，庶防秋時沿江號令歸一，可以固守。」

translations.literal: Ningzhi said: "Jingkou controls the great river and is the gateway of Western Zhe. I ask that Changzhou, Jiangyin Army, and the two counties Kunshan and Changshu be placed under this commission, so that in autumn defense along the river commands are unified and the line can be firmly held."
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi argued: "Jingkou commands the Yangtze and guards Western Zhe. Transfer Changzhou, Jiangyin, Kunshan, and Changshu to this command so autumn river defense speaks with one voice and the line holds firm."

sentences.zh: 權戶部侍郎，總領三宣撫司錢糧。

translations.literal: He was acting vice minister of revenue and overall supervisor of funds and grain for the three pacification commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of revenue, supervising funds for the three pacification commissions.

sentences.zh: 張浚都督諸軍，以為行府屬。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, as overall commander of the armies, made him staff officer of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commander Zhang Jun made him a staff officer at field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎，進徽猷閣直學士、知秀州，升顯謨閣，提舉太平觀，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of personnel, advanced to Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning and prefect of Xiuzhou, promoted to the Hall of Manifest Counsel, made Administrator of the Taiping Abbey, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Made vice minister of personnel, Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning, and prefect of Xiuzhou, he rose to the Hall of Manifest Counsel, administered the Taiping Abbey, and died.

sentences.zh: 寧止有文名，慷慨喜論事。

translations.literal: Ningzhi had a literary reputation and was generous, delighting in discussing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi was known for letters and spoke boldly on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 當艱難時，上疏言闕失，指切隱微，多人所難言。

translations.literal: In hard times he submitted memorials on omissions, pointing directly at hidden matters—much that others found hard to say.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis he memorialized on failures of state, naming hidden wrongs others dared not voice.

sentences.zh: 乞禁王安石《日錄》，復賢良方正科，用司馬光十科薦士法，仿唐制宰執論事以諫官侍立，皆其顯顯者。

translations.literal: He begged to ban Wang Anshi's Daily Record, restore the Exemplary and Upright subject category, use Sima Guang's Ten Categories method for recommending scholars, and follow Tang practice whereby chief ministers discussed affairs with remonstrance officials standing by—all prominent among his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He urged banning Wang Anshi's Daily Record, restoring the Exemplary and Upright examination, adopting Sima Guang's ten-category recommendation system, and reviving Tang practice of remonstrance officers attending council debates—among his best-known proposals.

sentences.zh: 勤王之舉，呂頤浩紀其有輸忠贊謀之勞。

translations.literal: In the loyalist enterprise Lü Yihao recorded his labor in loyal counsel and planning.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao credited his loyal counsel during the loyalist campaign.

sentences.zh: 寧止與一止、岑皆群從昆弟，帝嘗稱寧止忠、一止清、岑敏云。

translations.literal: Ningzhi with Yizhi and Cen were all cousins; the emperor once praised Ningzhi as loyal, Yizhi as pure, and Cen as keen.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi, Yizhi, and Cen were cousins; the emperor once praised Ningzhi's loyalty, Yizhi's integrity, and Cen's sharpness.

sentences.zh: 有《教忠堂類稿》十卷。

translations.literal: He had ten juan of the Jiaozhong Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left ten juan of the Jiaozhong Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 胡交修

translations.literal: Hu Jiaoxiu
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jiaoxiu

sentences.zh: 胡交修，字已楙，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Jiaoxiu, courtesy name Yimao, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jiaoxiu, styled Yimao, came from Jinling in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧二年進士第，授泰州推官，試詞學兼茂科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chongning, was appointed magistrate of Taizhou, and tested for the erudite letters and flourishing literature category.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the jinshi in the second year of Chongning (1103), he became magistrate of Taizhou and tested for erudite letters and flourishing literature.

sentences.zh: 給事中翟汝文同知貢舉，得其文曰：「非吾所能及也。」

translations.literal: Supervising drafter Zhai Ruwen, as co-director of the examinations, obtained his essay and said: "This is beyond what I can match."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising drafter Zhai Ruwen, co-directing the examination, read his paper and declared: "I cannot equal this."

sentences.zh: 置之首選，除編類國朝會要所檢閱文字。

translations.literal: He was placed first and appointed reviser of texts for the Compilation of Song Dynasty Institutional Compendia.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first and was made reviser for the Compilation of Song Dynasty Institutional Compendia.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，遷太常博士、都官郎，徙祠部，遷左司官，拜起居舍人、起居郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and director in the Ministry of Justice, moved to the Ministry of Rites, transferred to the Left Department, and appointed diarist-attendant and diarist.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 6 he became Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and director in the Ministry of Justice, then moved through the Ministries of Rites and the Left Department to diarist-attendant and diarist.

sentences.zh: 昭慈太后垂簾聽政，除右文殿修撰、知湖州。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhaoci held the curtain and heard government, he was appointed compiler of the Hall of Right Culture and prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhaoci regented, he was made compiler of the Hall of Right Culture and prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，以中書舍人召，辭不至，改徽猷閣待制、提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he was summoned as Secretariat drafter, declined and did not come, and was changed to vice director of the Hall of Splendid Learning and Administrator of the Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he was summoned as Secretariat drafter but declined, and was instead made vice director of the Hall of Splendid Learning and administrator of the Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，復以舍人召，詔守臣津發，尋進給事中、直學士院兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again summoned as drafter; an edict ordered local officials to provide escort. Soon he was advanced to supervising drafter, the Direct Academy, and concurrently court expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled as drafter; local officials were ordered to escort him. He soon became supervising drafter, entered the Direct Academy, and served as court expositor.

sentences.zh: 入對，首論天下大勢曰：「淮南當吾膺，將士遇敵先奔，無藩籬之衛。

translations.literal: Entering audience he first discussed the great situation of the realm: "Huainan is our chest—troops and generals flee before the enemy; we have no barrier defense.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he first surveyed the realm: "Huainan is our breastworks, yet troops flee at contact—we have no shield.

sentences.zh: 湖、廣帶吾脅，群盜乘間竊發，有腹心之憂。

translations.literal: Hunan and Guangdong flank our ribs—bandits rise in the gaps, and we have the worry of the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Guangdong press our flanks—bandits exploit every opening, threatening our vitals.

sentences.zh: 江、浙肇吾基，根本久未立。

translations.literal: Jiangsu and Zhejiang began our foundation—the root has long not been established.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu and Zhejiang were our foundation—yet the root was never firmly planted.

sentences.zh: 秦、蜀張吾援，指臂不相救。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Sichuan extend our arms—finger and arm do not rescue each other.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Sichuan are our arms—yet they cannot aid one another.

sentences.zh: 宜詔二三大臣修政事，選將帥，蒐補卒乘，以張國勢，撫綏疲瘵，以固國本。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should decree that two or three great ministers reform government, select generals, gather and replenish soldiers and chariots to expand national strength, and soothe the exhausted and afflicted to solidify the national foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Summon two or three senior ministers to reform government, choose generals, rebuild armies, expand national strength, and heal the exhausted to secure the state's foundation."

sentences.zh: 帝又出手詔，訪以弭盜保民、豐財裕國、強兵禦戎之要，交修疏言：

translations.literal: The emperor also issued a handwritten edict inquiring into the essentials of quelling bandits and protecting the people, enriching revenues and enlarging the state, and strengthening armies to guard against barbarians. Jiaoxiu submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also issued a handwritten edict asking how to suppress bandits, protect the people, enrich the treasury, and strengthen defenses. Jiaoxiu replied:

sentences.zh: 「昔人謂甑有麥飯，床有故絮，雖儀、秦說之不能使為盜，惟其凍餓無聊，日與死迫，然後忍以其身棄之于盜賊。

translations.literal: "The ancients said: if the cauldron has wheat gruel and the bed has old cotton, even Yi and Qin could not persuade one to become a bandit—only when frozen and starving with nothing to do, pressed daily toward death, does one endure casting oneself among bandits.
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients said: with gruel in the pot and cotton on the bed, even persuaders like Su Qin could not drive men to banditry—only when cold, hungry, and daily facing death do people throw in with robbers.

sentences.zh: 陛下下寬大之詔，開其自新之路，禁苛慝之暴，豐其衣食之源，則悔悟者更相告語歡呼而歸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has issued edicts of leniency, opening the path of self-renewal, forbidding harsh and cruel oppression, and enriching the sources of clothing and food—then those who repent will tell one another in joy and return.
translations.idiomatic: Issue lenient edicts, open paths to repentance, forbid cruel oppression, and secure livelihoods—then repentant men will return rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 其不變者，黨與攜落，亦為吏士所係獲，而盜可弭，盜弭則可以保民矣。

translations.literal: Those who do not change—their factions scatter and fall away, and they are also seized by officials and soldiers; bandits can be quelled, and when bandits are quelled the people can be protected.
translations.idiomatic: Holdouts will see their gangs collapse and be seized by officials; banditry will end, and with it the people will be safe.

sentences.zh: 沃野千里，殘為盜區，皆吾秔稻之地。

translations.literal: A thousand li of fertile fields lie ruined as bandit territory—all our rice paddies.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li of fertile land lies wasted to bandits—all once our rice country.

sentences.zh: 操弓矢，帶刀劍，椎牛發塚，白晝為盜，皆吾南畝之民。

translations.literal: Drawing bows, bearing swords, butchering cattle and opening graves, robbing by daylight—all our farmers in the southern fields.
translations.idiomatic: Men who draw bows, bear swords, slaughter cattle, and rob graves by daylight were once our farmers.

sentences.zh: 陛下撫而納之，反其田里，無急征暴斂，啟其不肖之心，耕桑以時，各安其業，穀帛不可勝用，而財可豐，財豐則可以裕國矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty soothes and accepts them, returns them to their fields, does not urgently levy or violently expropriate, opens the hearts of the unworthy, plows and mulberries in season, each secure in his occupation—grain and silk cannot be exhausted in use, and revenues can be enriched; when revenues are enriched the state can be enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: Welcome them back to their fields, levy lightly, let them farm in season, and each man keep his trade—grain and cloth will abound, the treasury will fill, and the state grow rich.

sentences.zh: 日者翟興連西路，董平據南楚，什伍其人，為農為兵，不數年，積粟充牣，雄視一方。

translations.literal: Recently Zhai Xing connected the western route and Dong Ping held southern Chu; they organized their people in fives and tens as farmers and soldiers. In not many years grain filled the stores and they dominated a region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Xing held the west and Dong Ping southern Chu; they organized men as farmers and soldiers, and within years their granaries overflowed and they dominated their regions.

sentences.zh: 盜賊猶能爾，況以中興二百郡地，欲強兵以禦寇，不能為翟興輩之所為乎？」

translations.literal: If bandits can do this, how much more the two hundred commanderies of the Restoration—wishing to strengthen armies to guard against invaders, can we not do what men like Zhai Xing have done?"
translations.idiomatic: If bandits can manage this, cannot the Restoration's two hundred prefectures, seeking strong armies against invaders, do as Zhai Xing did?"

sentences.zh: 世以為名言。

translations.literal: The age considered these famous words.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries hailed these as words of wisdom.

sentences.zh: 李成盜江、淮，廷議欲親征，交修謂：「群盜猖狂，天子自將，勝之則不武，不勝則貽天下笑。

translations.literal: Li Cheng plundered the Jiang-Huai region. Court discussion wished the emperor to campaign in person. Jiaoxiu said: "The bandits are reckless; if the Son of Heaven leads in person, victory is unbecoming, defeat would be laughed at by the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cheng ravaged the Jiang-Huai, court debate favored an imperial campaign. Jiaoxiu objected: "Petty bandits run wild—if the Son of Heaven leads in person, victory is unworthy and defeat a national disgrace.

sentences.zh: 此將帥之責，何足以辱王師？」

translations.literal: This is the generals' responsibility—how could it be enough to humiliate the royal army?"
translations.idiomatic: This is work for generals—why demean the imperial host?"

sentences.zh: 議遂格，盜尋遁。

translations.literal: The discussion was blocked; the bandits soon fled.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped; the bandits soon dispersed.

sentences.zh: 周杞守常州，坐殘虐免。

translations.literal: Zhou Qi defended Changzhou and was dismissed for cruelty and oppression.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi, prefect of Changzhou, was dismissed for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，帝問交修致旱之由，對以殆杞佚罰之故，乃以杞屬吏。

translations.literal: When a great drought came the emperor asked Jiaoxiu the cause of the drought. He replied that it was probably because Qi had evaded punishment; Qi was then turned over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: During severe drought the emperor asked Jiaoxiu the cause. He answered that Qi had escaped punishment; Qi was handed to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 杞疑為交修所讒，上書告其罪，遣大理寺丞胡蒙詣常按驗。

translations.literal: Qi suspected he had been slandered by Jiaoxiu, submitted a memorial reporting his crimes, and the Court of Judicial Review sent assistant magistrate Hu Meng to Changzhou to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Qi suspected Jiaoxiu had slandered him, accused Jiaoxiu by memorial, and the Court of Judicial Review sent Hu Meng to Changzhou to investigate.

sentences.zh: 交修無所絓，然群從多抵罪。

translations.literal: Jiaoxiu was not implicated, yet many of his clan were convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxiu was cleared, but many kinsmen were convicted.

sentences.zh: 尋以徽猷閣待制提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice director of the Hall of Splendid Learning and Administrator of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Hall of Splendid Learning and administrator of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 六年，召為給事中、刑部侍郎、翰林學士、知制誥兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as supervising drafter, vice minister of punishments, Hanlin academician, drafter of edicts, and concurrently court reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled as supervising drafter, vice minister of punishments, Hanlin academician, edict drafter, and court reader.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After long service he was transferred to minister of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he became minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 汀州寧化縣論大辟十人，獄已上，知州事鄭強驗問，無一人當死，交修乞治縣令冒賞殺無辜罪。

translations.literal: In Ninghua County, Tingzhou, ten persons were sentenced to capital punishment; the case had been submitted. Prefect Zheng Qiang reviewed the interrogations and not one deserved death. Jiaoxiu begged punishment for the county magistrate's crime of seeking reward by killing the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: In Ninghua County, Tingzhou, ten men were sentenced to death; Prefect Zheng Qiang found none deserved it. Jiaoxiu demanded punishment for the magistrate who killed innocents for reward.

sentences.zh: 江東留獄追逮者尚六百人，交修言：「若待六百人俱至，則瘐死者眾矣，請以罪狀明白者論如律，疑則從輕。」

translations.literal: In Jiangdong more than six hundred persons still awaited trial in detention. Jiaoxiu said: "If we wait until all six hundred arrive, many will die in prison. I ask that those whose guilt is clear be judged by law, and where there is doubt, leniency be applied."
translations.idiomatic: More than six hundred detainees still awaited trial in Jiangdong. Jiaoxiu urged: "Waiting for all six hundred means many will die in custody. Judge clear cases by law; where doubt remains, show mercy."

sentences.zh: 詔皆如其言。

translations.literal: Edicts all followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 朝論欲以四川交子行之諸路，交修力陳其害，謂：「崇寧大錢覆轍可鑒，當時大臣建議，人皆附和，未幾錢分兩等，市有二價，姦民盜鑄，死徙相屬。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to extend Sichuan's jiaozi notes to all circuits. Jiaoxiu forcefully set forth the harm and said: "The Chongning large-coin debacle is a lesson. Then great ministers proposed it and all echoed; before long the coin split into two grades, the market had two prices, wicked men counterfeited, and death and exile followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate favored extending Sichuan's jiaozi paper notes empire-wide. Jiaoxiu warned: "The Chongning large-coin disaster is warning enough—ministers proposed it, all agreed, and soon coins split in value, markets doubled in price, counterfeiters flourished, and death and exile followed.

sentences.zh: 以今交子校之大錢，無銅炭之費，無鼓鑄之勞，一夫挾紙日作十數萬，真贗莫辨，售之不疑，一觸憲網，破家壞產，以賞告捕，禍及無辜。

translations.literal: Comparing today's jiaozi to the large coin—without copper and charcoal expense, without smelting labor—a single man with paper can make hundreds of thousands in a day; true and false cannot be distinguished, sold without doubt; one touch of the law and family and property are ruined, rewards for informing reach the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with large coins, jiaozi need no copper or smelting—one man with paper can print hundreds of thousands daily, real and fake indistinguishable. One brush with the law destroys families; informers' rewards harm the innocent.

sentences.zh: 歲月之後，公私之錢盡歸藏鏹之家，商賈不行，市井蕭條，比及悔悟，恐無及矣。」

translations.literal: After months and years public and private money will all go to hoarders' coffers; merchants will not circulate and markets will be desolate—by the time of repentance I fear it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: In time all money will sit in hoarders' vaults, trade will halt, markets wither—and repentance will come too late."

sentences.zh: 時議大舉，交修曰：「今妄言無行之徒，為迎合可喜之論，吾無以考驗其實，遽信之以舉事，豈不誤國哉？」

translations.literal: At the time discussion was widespread. Jiaoxiu said: "Today reckless men without conduct, to offer pleasing talk that flatters— I have no means to verify the reality, yet believe them at once and act—is this not misleading the state?"
translations.idiomatic: With the proposal widely favored, Jiaoxiu said: "Flatterers offer pleasing schemes I cannot verify—shall we trust them and act, and so mislead the state?"

sentences.zh: 帝覽之矍然。

translations.literal: The emperor, reading it, was startled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and started.

sentences.zh: 翌日，出其奏示大臣曰：「交修真一士之諤諤也。」

translations.literal: The next day he produced the memorial and showed the great ministers, saying: "Jiaoxiu is truly a lone loyal voice."
translations.idiomatic: Next day he showed the memorial to his ministers: "Jiaoxiu is a lone honest voice."

sentences.zh: 蜀帥席益既去，帝問交修孰可守蜀者，對以臣從子世將可用，遂以世將為樞密直學士、四川安撫制置使。

translations.literal: When Sichuan commander Xi Yi had departed, the emperor asked Jiaoxiu who could guard Shu. He replied that his clansman Shijiang was usable; Shijiang was then made direct academician of the Military Affairs Commission and Sichuan pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan commander Xi Yi left office, the emperor asked who could hold Shu. Jiaoxiu named his kinsman Shijiang, who was made direct academician of the Military Affairs Commission and Sichuan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世將在蜀五年，號為名帥。

translations.literal: Shijiang was in Shu five years and was called a famous commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiang governed Shu five years and was reckoned a fine commander.

sentences.zh: 自重兵聚關外以守蜀，餉道險遠，漕舟自嘉陵江而上，春夏漲而多覆，秋冬涸而多膠。

translations.literal: Because heavy troops gathered outside the passes to guard Shu, the supply route was dangerous and distant; transport boats went up the Jialing River—in spring and summer when it swelled many capsized, in autumn and winter when it ran dry many stuck on shoals.
translations.idiomatic: With main forces massed beyond the passes, supply lines were long and perilous. Barges on the Jialing capsized in spring floods and grounded in autumn drought.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，宣撫副使吳玠始行陸運，調成都、潼川、利州三路夫十萬，縣官部送，徼賞爭先，十斃三四。

translations.literal: In the early Shaoxing era Vice Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie first instituted overland transport, mobilizing one hundred thousand corvée laborers from the three circuits of Chengdu, Tongchuan, and Lizhou; county officials escorted them competing for reward; of ten, three or four died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing, Vice Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie began overland transport, drafting a hundred thousand laborers from Chengdu, Tongchuan, and Lizhou; officials raced for credit and three or four in ten died.

sentences.zh: 至是交修言：「養兵所以保蜀也，民不堪命則腹心先潰，何以保蜀？

translations.literal: At this Jiaoxiu said: "Maintaining soldiers is to protect Shu. If the people cannot bear the burden then the heart and belly first collapses—how can Shu be protected?
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxiu warned: "Armies exist to guard Shu—if the people break, the heart collapses first. How then guard Shu?

sentences.zh: 臣愚欲三月以後、九月以前，第存守關正兵，餘悉就糧他州，如此則守關者水運可給，分戍者陸運可免。」

translations.literal: I foolishly wish that from the third month onward until before the ninth month, only the regular troops guarding the passes be kept; all the rest take grain in other prefectures—thus those guarding the passes can be supplied by water transport, and those garrisoned elsewhere can be spared overland transport."
translations.idiomatic: From the third month through the eighth, keep only garrison troops at the passes; send the rest to draw grain elsewhere—pass garrisons supplied by water, outposts spared overland hauls."

sentences.zh: 帝命學士院述交修意，詔玠行之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Academy to set forth Jiaoxiu's intent, and an edict ordered Jie to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the Academy draft Jiaoxiu's plan into edict; Wu Jie was ordered to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 議徽宗配享功臣，交修奏：「韓忠彥建中靖國初為相，賢譽翕然，時號『小元祐』。」

translations.literal: Discussing posthumous enfeoffment of meritorious ministers with Emperor Huizong, Jiaoxiu memorialized: "Han Zhongyan became chief minister at the beginning of the Jianzhong Jingguo era; worthy reputation gathered, and the age called him 'Little Yuanyou.'
translations.idiomatic: Debating Huizong's posthumous honors for meritorious ministers, Jiaoxiu argued: "Han Zhongyan became chief minister at the opening of Jianzhong Jingguo; acclaim gathered, and men called him 'Little Yuanyou.'"

sentences.zh: 從之，人大允服。

translations.literal: It was followed; people greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed; public opinion approved.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，以親老，除寶文閣學士、知信州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, summer, because his parent was old he was appointed academician of the Hall of Precious Culture and prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, summer, citing an aged parent, he was made academician of the Hall of Precious Culture and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，上欲留侍經筵，力言母老，願奉祠里中以便養。

translations.literal: Entering to take leave, the emperor wished to retain him to serve the classics lecture; he forcefully said his mother was old and wished to receive an abbey appointment in his home district for convenient support.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of court, he declined the emperor's wish to keep him at the classics lecture, pleading an aged mother and requesting a home abbey for her care.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿去，行復召矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When you leave, I will summon you again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Go now—I will call you back."

sentences.zh: 改提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年六月召還，除兵部尚書、翰林學士兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, sixth month, he was recalled, appointed minister of war, Hanlin academician, and concurrently court expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, sixth month, he was recalled as minister of war, Hanlin academician, and court expositor.

sentences.zh: 時河南新復，交修奏；

translations.literal: At the time Henan had newly been recovered; Jiaoxiu memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: With Henan newly recovered, Jiaoxiu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「京西、陝右取士之法，乞如祖宗時設諸科之目，以待西北之士；

translations.literal: "For selecting scholars in Jingxi and Shaanxi-right, I beg that examination categories be established as in the times of the ancestors to await scholars of the northwest;
translations.idiomatic: "For recruiting in Jingxi and western Shaanxi, restore the ancestral examination categories for northwestern scholars;

sentences.zh: 別為號於南宮，以收五路之才。」

translations.literal: separately establish designations at the southern palace to gather talent from the five circuits."
translations.idiomatic: create separate palace examination tracks to gather talent from the five circuits."

sentences.zh: 詔令禮部討論。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to study the proposal.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復請補外，除端明殿學士、知合州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again requested an outside appointment and was made academician of the Hall of Manifest Counsel and prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he sought an outside post and became academician of the Hall of Manifest Counsel and prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 卻私請，免上供以萬計，領州數月卒。

translations.literal: He refused private requests and exempted tribute payments numbering in the tens of thousands; after several months governing the prefecture he died.
translations.idiomatic: He refused private favors, waived tribute payments in the tens of thousands, and died after only months as prefect.

sentences.zh: 交修簡重寡言，進止有度，為文不事琢雕，坦然明白，在詞苑號為稱職。

translations.literal: Jiaoxiu was simple and grave, sparing of words, with measured advance and withdrawal. In writing he did not pursue carving and polish; plainly and clearly—within the literary garden he was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaoxiu was reserved and measured, sparing in speech, writing plainly without ornament—well regarded among literary officials.

sentences.zh: 自其從祖宿、從父宗愈至交修、世將，皆在禁林。

translations.literal: From his great-uncle Su, his father's brother Zongyu, down to Jiaoxiu and Shijiang—all were in the Forbidden Grove.
translations.idiomatic: From his great-uncle Su and uncle Zongyu through Jiaoxiu and Shijiang, the family served in the Forbidden Grove.

sentences.zh: 中興以後，學士三入者自交修始。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, entering the academy three times began with Jiaoxiu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, Jiaoxiu was the first to enter the Hanlin Academy three times.

sentences.zh: 交修裒次為書，號《四世絲綸集》，以侈一門之遇。

translations.literal: Jiaoxiu compiled a book called Four Generations of Imperial Edicts, to display one family's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Four Generations of Imperial Edicts to celebrate the family's imperial service.

sentences.zh: 至於事繼母以孝聞，撫二弟極其友愛，遇恩以次補官，若交修者，其文行之兼副者歟！

translations.literal: As for serving his stepmother with filial fame, cherishing two younger brothers with utmost brotherly love, and receiving favor in order to supplement offices for kin—if such as Jiaoxiu, is this not one in whom literary and conduct both measure up!
translations.idiomatic: Filial to a stepmother, devoted to two younger brothers, passing favors to kin in proper order—was Jiaoxiu not a man whose letters and conduct alike measured up?

sentences.zh: 綦崇禮

translations.literal: Qi Chongli
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongli

sentences.zh: 綦崇禮，字叔厚，高密人，後徙濰之北海。

translations.literal: Qi Chongli, courtesy name Shuhou, was a native of Gaomi; later he moved to Beihai in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongli, styled Shuhou, was from Gaomi and later moved to Beihai in Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖及父皆中明經進士科。

translations.literal: Both grandfather and father passed the Mingjing jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather and father both passed the Mingjing jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禮幼穎邁，十歲能作邑人墓銘，父見大驚曰：「吾家積善之報，其在茲乎！」

translations.literal: Chongli in youth was sharp and surpassing; at ten sui he could compose an epitaph for a townsman. His father, greatly startled, said: "The reward of our family's accumulated goodness—is it in this!"
translations.idiomatic: Precocious as a boy, at ten he wrote a townsman's epitaph. His father marveled: "Our family's accumulated virtue bears fruit here!"

sentences.zh: 初入太學，諸生溺于王氏新說，少能詞藝者。

translations.literal: When he first entered the Imperial College, students were drowned in the Wang clan's New Learning; few could compose polished prose.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Imperial College, students were steeped in Wang Anshi's New Learning and few could write polished prose.

sentences.zh: 徽宗幸太學，崇禮出二表，祭酒與同列大稱其工。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong visited the Imperial College; Chongli produced two memorials. The libationer and colleagues greatly praised their craftsmanship.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong visited the college, Chongli submitted two memorials that the libationer and fellows praised as masterly.

sentences.zh: 登重和元年上舍第，調淄縣主簿，為太學正，遷博士，改宣教郎、秘書省正字，除工部員外郎，尋為起居郎、攝給事中。

translations.literal: He passed the shangshe examination in the first year of Chonghe, was appointed chief clerk of Zi County, became director of the Imperial College, was transferred to Erudite, changed to Gentleman for Spreading the Teachings and rectifier of texts in the Secretariat, appointed vice director in the Ministry of Works, and soon became diarist and acting supervising drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the shangshe examination in Chonghe 1, he served as chief clerk of Zi County, director and then Erudite of the Imperial College, rectifier in the Secretariat, vice director in the Ministry of Works, then diarist and acting supervising drafter.

sentences.zh: 召試政事堂，為制誥三篇，不淹晷而就，辭翰奇偉。

translations.literal: Summoned to test at the Hall of Administration, he composed three edicts; without the span of a shadow he finished—his literary brush was singular and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Tested at the Hall of Administration, he drafted three edicts in a breath—his prose singular and grand.

sentences.zh: 拜中書舍人，賜三品服，進用之速，近世所未有，高宗猶以為得之晚。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat drafter and granted third-rank robes. The speed of promotion was unmatched in recent generations; Gaozong still thought he had obtained him late.
translations.idiomatic: Made Secretariat drafter with third-rank robes, he rose faster than any in recent memory—yet Gaozong still felt he had come late.

sentences.zh: 車駕如平江，有旨鄒浩追復龍圖閣待制，崇禮當行詞，推帝所以褒恤遺直之意，有曰：「處心不欺，養氣至大。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Pingjiang, an edict ordered Zou Hao posthumously restored to vice director of the Dragon Diagram Hall. Chongli was to draft the edict; he extended the emperor's intent to praise and comfort the upright remnant, saying: "His heart without deceit, his spirit cultivated to greatness.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Pingjiang, an edict restored Zou Hao posthumously to vice director of the Dragon Diagram Hall. Chongli drafted the text, voicing the emperor's praise for the martyred upright: "A heart without deceit, a spirit cultivated to greatness.

sentences.zh: 言期寤意，引裾嘗犯于雷霆；

translations.literal: His words expected to awaken the sovereign's mind; he once grasped the robe and offended the thunder of imperial wrath;
translations.idiomatic: His words sought to awaken the throne; he once seized the emperor's robe and braved imperial thunder—

sentences.zh: 計不顧身，去國再遷於嶺徼。

translations.literal: his plans disregarded his person; twice he was banished from the state to the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: his plans scorned self-preservation; twice exile sent him to the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 群臣動色，志士傾心。」

translations.literal: Ministers changed color; men of resolve bent their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers paled; men of resolve bowed their hearts."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「英爽不忘，想生氣之猶在；

translations.literal: He also said: "His bright spirit is not forgotten—I think his living breath is still present;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "His bright spirit is not forgotten—living breath seems still to linger;

sentences.zh: 姦諛已死，知朽骨之尚寒。」

translations.literal: flattery and sycophancy are already dead—I know even their rotten bones are still cold."
translations.idiomatic: flatterers lie dead—even their rotten bones still chill the air."

sentences.zh: 同列推重，除試尚書吏部侍郎，時從官惟崇禮與汪藻，尋兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Colleagues esteemed him. He was appointed acting vice minister of personnel in the Ministry of Civil Office; at the time among attendants only Chongli and Wang Zao; soon he also held the Direct Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues admired the draft. He became acting vice minister of personnel; among attendants only he and Wang Zao remained—soon he also held the Direct Academy.

sentences.zh: 以徽猷閣直學士知漳州，其俗悍強，號難治，屬有巨寇起建州，聲撼鄰境，人心動搖，崇禮牧民禦眾，一如常日，訖盜息，環城內外按堵如故。

translations.literal: As Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning he was prefect of Zhangzhou. Its customs were fierce and strong, called hard to govern. At the time a great bandit rose in Jianzhou; his fame shook neighboring territories; people's hearts wavered. Chongli governed the people and controlled the multitude just as on ordinary days; when the bandits ceased the city inside and outside the walls was as calm as before.
translations.idiomatic: As Direct Aide of the Hall of Splendid Learning and prefect of Zhangzhou—renowned for fierce customs and hard rule—he faced a great bandit in Jianzhou whose fame shook the region. Chongli governed as on any other day; when banditry ended, the city within and without remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 徙知明州，召為吏部侍郎兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Mingzhou and summoned as vice minister of personnel and concurrently acting director of the Direct Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Mingzhou, he was recalled as vice minister of personnel and acting director of the Direct Academy.

sentences.zh: 時有詔侍從官日輪一員，具前代及本朝事關治體者一二事進入，崇禮言：「祖宗以來選用儒臣，以奉講讀。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered attendants to rotate daily, each submitting one or two matters from former ages and this dynasty relating to governance. Chongli said: "Since the ancestors, Confucian officials have been selected to serve lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required attendants to rotate daily, each submitting one or two cases from past and present bearing on governance. Chongli objected: "Since the ancestors, Confucian officials were chosen to lecture and read.

sentences.zh: 若令從官一例獻其所聞，既非舊典，且又越職，望令講讀官三五日一進。」

translations.literal: If attendants are uniformly made to offer what they have heard, it is neither the old statute nor their office. I hope lecture and reading officials may submit every three or five days."
translations.idiomatic: Making all attendants report what they hear is neither old practice nor their duty. Let lecture and reading officials submit every three to five days."

sentences.zh: 乃命學士與兩省官如前詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon academicians and officials of the two provinces were ordered as in the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians and officials of the two provinces were ordered as before.

sentences.zh: 又言：「駐蹕臨安，以浙西為根本，宜固江、淮之守，然後可以圖興復。

translations.literal: He also said: "The court is stationed at Lin'an; with Western Zhe as foundation, the defense of the Jiang and Huai should be secured—and then recovery can be planned.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Stationed at Lin'an with Western Zhe as foundation, secure the Jiang-Huai line—then plan recovery.

sentences.zh: 蜀在萬里外，當召用其士夫，慰安遠人之心。」

translations.literal: Shu is ten thousand li away; its scholar-officials should be summoned and employed to soothe the hearts of distant men."
translations.idiomatic: Shu lies ten thousand li distant—summon its scholar-officials to reassure those far from court."

sentences.zh: 時兵革後，省曹簿書殘毀幾盡，崇禮再執銓法，熟於典故，討論沿革，援據該審，吏不得容其私。

translations.literal: At the time after the military upheaval, provincial bureau ledgers and documents were ruined almost entirely. Chongli again wielded appointment law; versed in precedents, he discussed origins and changes, citing evidence comprehensively—clerks could not harbor private ends.
translations.idiomatic: After war, provincial records lay nearly destroyed. Chongli again enforced appointment law, versed in precedent, tracing origins and changes with full citation—clerks could not cheat.

sentences.zh: 後有詔重刊七司條敕，崇禮所建明，悉著為令。

translations.literal: Later an edict reprinted the statutes of the Seven Bureaus; what Chongli had clarified was all written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Seven Bureaus' statutes were reprinted, Chongli's clarifications were all written into law.

sentences.zh: 移兵部侍郎，仍進直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of war and still advanced in the Direct Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to vice minister of war, he remained in the Direct Academy.

sentences.zh: 御筆處分召至都堂，令條具進討固守利害。

translations.literal: By imperial brush disposition he was summoned to the chief council hall and ordered to itemize and submit the pros and cons of advance and defense.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he was summoned to the chief council hall to itemize the pros and cons of advance and defense.

sentences.zh: 崇禮奏：「諜傳金人併兵趣川、陝，蓋以向來江左用兵非敵之便，故二三歲來悉力窺蜀。

translations.literal: Chongli memorialized: "Spy reports say the Jurchens are combining armies toward Chuan and Shaanxi—because using troops in the Jiang-left has not been the enemy's convenience, these two or three years they have exerted all strength to spy on Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli reported: "Spies say the Jurchens mass armies toward Sichuan and Shaanxi—finding the lower Yangtze ill-suited, these two or three years they have fixed on Shu.

sentences.zh: 其意以謂蜀若不守，江、浙自搖，故必圖之，非特報前日吳玠一敗而已。

translations.literal: Their intent is that if Shu is not held, Jiang and Zhe will shake of themselves—therefore they must plan for it; it is not merely to avenge Wu Jie's defeat of other days.
translations.idiomatic: They reckon that if Shu falls, Jiang and Zhe will shake—so they must take it; this is not merely revenge for Wu Jie's old defeat.

sentences.zh: 今日利害，在蜀兵之勝負。」

translations.literal: Today's advantage and harm lie in the victory and defeat of Shu troops."
translations.idiomatic: Today's stakes are victory or defeat in Shu."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「君之有臣，所以濟治。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "A ruler has ministers in order to complete governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "A ruler keeps ministers to finish the work of rule.

sentences.zh: 臣效實用，則君享其功；

translations.literal: If ministers effect practical use, the ruler enjoys the achievement;
translations.idiomatic: When ministers deliver real service, the ruler gains the credit;

sentences.zh: 臣竊虛名，則君受其弊。

translations.literal: if ministers steal empty fame, the ruler suffers the harm.
translations.idiomatic: when ministers steal empty fame, the ruler bears the harm.

sentences.zh: 實用之利在國，虛名之美在身。

translations.literal: The benefit of practical use is for the state; the beauty of empty fame is for the person.
translations.idiomatic: Real service benefits the state; empty fame beautifies the self.

sentences.zh: 忠於國者，不計一己之毀譽，惟天下之治亂是憂；

translations.literal: Those loyal to the state do not calculate their own slander and praise—only the order and disorder of the realm do they worry about;
translations.idiomatic: Men loyal to the realm ignore personal praise and blame and worry only for order and chaos;

sentences.zh: 潔其身者，不顧天下之治亂，惟一己之毀譽是恤。

translations.literal: those who polish themselves do not care for the order and disorder of the realm—only their own slander and praise do they cherish.
translations.idiomatic: men who polish themselves ignore order and chaos and cherish only their own reputation.

sentences.zh: 然效力于國，其實甚難，世未必貴；

translations.literal: Yet serving with effect for the state is in reality very hard, and the age does not necessarily honor it;
translations.idiomatic: Serving the state truly is hard, and the age may not honor it;

sentences.zh: 竊名於己，其為則易，且以得譽。

translations.literal: stealing fame for oneself is easy in practice, and one moreover obtains praise.
translations.idiomatic: stealing fame is easy, and praise follows.

sentences.zh: 二者有關於風俗甚大，是不可不察也。」

translations.literal: The two have great relation to custom—this cannot but be examined."
translations.idiomatic: Both weigh heavily on custom—this cannot go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 九月，御筆除翰林學士，自靖康後，從官以御筆除拜自此始。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, by imperial brush he was appointed Hanlin academician. From Jingkang onward, appointment of attendants by imperial brush began here.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an imperial brush made him Hanlin academician—the first such appointment since Jingkang.

sentences.zh: 楊惟忠、邢煥以節度使致仕，告由舍人院出，崇禮言：「祖宗時，凡節鉞臣僚得謝，不以文武，並納節別除一官致仕。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong and Xing Huan, as military commissioners, requested retirement; the announcement came from the drafters' office. Chongli said: "In the times of the ancestors, whenever military commissioners received dismissal, without regard to civil or military, all surrendered their seals and were separately appointed to an office in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong and Xing Huan retired as military commissioners; the announcement came from the drafters' office. Chongli noted: "Under the ancestors, commissioners surrendering seals were reappointed to retirement posts, civil or military alike.

sentences.zh: 熙寧間，富弼以元勳始令特帶節鉞致仕，其後繼者曾公亮、文彥博，他人豈可援以為例。」

translations.literal: In the Xining era Fu Bi, as founding minister, was first ordered specially to retire while retaining seals; afterward successors Zeng Gongliang and Wen Yanbo—how could others cite this as precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: In Xining Fu Bi, a founding minister, was first allowed to retire keeping his seal; later Zeng Gongliang and Wen Yanbo followed—others should not cite this."

sentences.zh: 詔自今如祖宗故典。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on the old statutes of the ancestors be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts restored the ancestral rule.

sentences.zh: 進兼侍讀兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrently court reader and compiler of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to court reader and History Office compiler.

sentences.zh: 時有旨重修神宗、哲宗《正史》。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered revision of the Correct Histories of Shenzong and Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered revision of the Correct Histories of Shenzong and Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 兵火之後，典籍散亡，崇禮奏：「《神宗實錄》墨本，元祐所修已是成書，朱本出蔡卞手，多所附會，乞將朱墨本參照修定。

translations.literal: After the fires of war, canonical works were scattered and lost. Chongli memorialized: "The ink manuscript of the Veritable Records of Shenzong—what Yuanyou compiled was already a completed book; the Zhu manuscript came from Cai Bian's hand and in many places was attached and joined. I beg that the Zhu and ink manuscripts be compared and revised.
translations.idiomatic: After war scattered the archives, Chongli reported: "Shenzong's Veritable Records exist in ink and Zhu manuscripts—the Yuanyou ink text is complete; Cai Bian's Zhu text is tendentious. Compare and revise both.

sentences.zh: 《哲宗實錄》，崇寧間蔡京提舉編修，增飾語言，變亂是非，難以便據舊錄修定，欲乞訪求故臣之家文獻事蹟參照。」

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Zhezong—in the Chongning era Cai Jing supervised compilation, embellishing language and confusing right and wrong; it is hard conveniently to revise according to the old record. I wish to beg to search the documentary traces and deeds in the homes of former ministers for comparison."
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong's Records, compiled under Cai Jing in Chongning, embellish and distort truth; the old text cannot simply be revised. Search former ministers' homes for documents to compare."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「知湖州汪藻編類元符庚辰至建炎己酉三十年事蹟，乞下藻以已成文字赴本所。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Wang Zao, prefect of Huzhou, compiled events from the Gengchen year of Yuanfu through the Jiyou year of Jianyan—thirty years of deeds. I beg that Zao be ordered to send completed text to this office."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Wang Zao, prefect of Huzhou, who had compiled thirty years of events from Yuanfu gengchen through Jianyan jiyou, submit his finished text."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，藻奉詔訪求甚備，未及修纂，崇禮取而專之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zao had received an edict to search with great completeness; before revision was completed Chongli took it and monopolized it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao had been ordered to search exhaustively; before he could finish, Chongli seized the project for himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗進唐太宗錄刺史姓名于屏風故事，曰：「連千里之封得一良守，則千里之民安；

translations.literal: He once submitted the story of Emperor Taizong recording prefects' names on a screen, saying: "Across a thousand li of territory, obtain one good governor and the people of a thousand li are secure;
translations.idiomatic: He once cited Taizong's practice of listing prefects' names on a screen: "One good governor over a thousand li secures a thousand li of people;

sentences.zh: 環百里之境得一良令，則百里之民說。

translations.literal: around a hundred li of territory, obtain one good magistrate and the people of a hundred li are pleased.
translations.idiomatic: one good magistrate over a hundred li pleases a hundred li of people.

sentences.zh: 牧民之吏咸得其良，則治功成矣。

translations.literal: If all administrators of the people obtain the good, then the work of governance is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When every local administrator is worthy, governance succeeds.

sentences.zh: 苟能效當時之事，以守令姓名詳列于屏，簡在帝心，則人知盡心職業。」

translations.literal: If we can effect the affairs of that time, listing prefects' and magistrates' names in detail on a screen, selected in the emperor's heart, then people will know to exhaust themselves in their duties."
translations.idiomatic: Revive that practice—list worthy prefects and magistrates on the imperial screen—and men will know to serve with their whole hearts."

sentences.zh: 再入翰林凡五年，所撰詔命數百篇，文簡意明，不私美，不寄怨，深得代言之體。

translations.literal: Entering the Hanlin a second time, in all five years he drafted several hundred edicts; the text was concise and the meaning clear, without private praise, without lodged resentment—deeply obtaining the style of speaking for another.
translations.idiomatic: In his second Hanlin tenure of five years he drafted hundreds of edicts—concise, clear, neither flattering nor vindictive—in the true voice of imperial words.

sentences.zh: 以寶文閣直學士知紹興府。

translations.literal: As Direct Aide of the Hall of Precious Culture he was prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Made Direct Aide of the Hall of Precious Culture, he governed Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 劉豫導金人入侵，揚、楚震擾，高宗躬御戎衣次吳會。

translations.literal: Liu Yu guided the Jurchens to invade; Yang and Chu were shaken and disturbed. Gaozong personally wore martial garb and halted at Wuhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu led Jurchen invasion, Yangzhou and Chuzhou trembled. Gaozong donned armor and halted at Wuhui.

sentences.zh: 崇禮以近臣承寧方面，謂浙東一道為行都肘腋之地，備禦不可不謹，密疏於朝，得便宜從事。

translations.literal: Chongli, as a close minister undertaking peace in his region, said that the Eastern Zhe circuit was the armpit of the mobile capital; defense could not but be careful. He submitted a secret memorial to court and obtained discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli, a close minister holding a frontier post, warned that Eastern Zhe was the capital's armpit and defense must be rigorous. A secret memorial won him discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 於是繕城郭，厲甲兵，輸錢帛以犒王師，簡舟艦以扼海道，疚心夙夜，殆廢食寢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired walls and moats, sharpened armor and weapons, sent money and silk to reward the royal army, selected boats and ships to control the sea route—his heart afflicted day and night, almost forgetting food and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired walls, honed arms, sent funds to reward the imperial army, and deployed ships to block the sea lanes—working day and night, nearly forgoing food and sleep.

sentences.zh: 及春，帝還，七州晏然不知羽檄之遽。

translations.literal: When spring came the emperor returned; the seven prefectures were calm and did not know the urgency of the dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: When spring brought the emperor's return, seven prefectures stayed calm, unaware how close war had come.

sentences.zh: 斯年，上印綬，退居台州。

translations.literal: That year he returned his seal and sash and retired to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he surrendered seal and sash and retired to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十，贈左朝議大夫。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty and was posthumously granted Left Court Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty and was posthumously made Left Court Counselor.

sentences.zh: 崇禮妙齡秀髮，聰敏絕人，不為崖岸斬絕之行。

translations.literal: Chongli in youth had elegant hair and was clever beyond others; he did not perform cliff-edge severed conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful and brilliant, he was clever beyond peers yet never aloof or harsh.

sentences.zh: 廉儉寡欲，獨覃心辭章，洞曉音律，酒酣氣振，長歌慷慨，議論風生，亦一時之英也。

translations.literal: Frugal and of few desires, he devoted himself solely to literary composition, thoroughly understood musical pitch; when wine warmed his spirit he sang long songs with passion, and when discussion stirred wind arose—he too was a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and ascetic, he devoted himself to letters and music; warmed by wine he sang boldly and debated with fire— a man of his age.

sentences.zh: 中年頓剉場屋，晚方登第，以縣主簿驟昇華要，極潤色論思之選。

translations.literal: In mid-life he suddenly failed in the examination halls; late he finally passed and from county chief clerk abruptly rose to the flowering peak, reaching the utmost choice for polishing discourse and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-career he languished in examinations; late he passed and rose from county clerk to the inner court, reaching the summit of deliberative drafting.

sentences.zh: 端方亮直，不憚強禦，秦檜罷政，崇禮草詞顯著其惡無所隱，檜深憾之。

translations.literal: Upright and bright, he did not fear the powerful. When Qin Hui was dismissed from government Chongli drafted the edict prominently showing his evil without concealment; Hui deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and fearless, when Qin Hui fell from power Chongli's draft edict exposed his crimes without concealment—Hui hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及再相，矯詔下台州就崇禮家索其稿，自於帝前納之，且將修怨。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister again he forged an edict sent to Taizhou to search Chongli's home for his drafts, personally receiving them before the emperor, and was about to settle old scores.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui returned to power he forged an edict searching Chongli's home in Taizhou for drafts, presented them before the emperor, and planned revenge.

sentences.zh: 會崇禮已沒，故身後所得恩澤，其家畏懼不敢陳，士大夫亦無敢為其任保。

translations.literal: Chongli had already died; therefore the posthumous favors his family received—they feared and did not state; scholar-officials also had none who dared act as guarantor for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli was already dead; his family's posthumous honors went unclaimed from fear, and no official dared stand guarantor.

sentences.zh: 樓鑰嘗敘其文，以為氣格渾然天成，一旦當書命之任，明白洞達，雖武夫遠人曉然知上意所在云。

translations.literal: Lou Yue once narrated his writings, considering their spirit and structure naturally formed; once entrusted with the duty of writing mandates, plainly and penetratingly—even military men and distant people clearly knew where the sovereign's intent lay.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yue praised his prose as naturally formed in spirit; entrusted with imperial words, he wrote so plainly that even soldiers and distant peoples knew the throne's intent.

sentences.zh: 論曰：建炎、紹興之際，網羅俊彥，布於庶職，如衛膚敏以下七人者，其論議時政，指陳闕失，雖或好惡多不同，亦皆一時之表表者，矧一止、甯止兄弟之忠清，交修、崇禮之祠翰，又有助於治化者焉。

translations.literal: The judgment says: In the Jianyan and Shaoxing era, the net gathered outstanding talents and spread them through myriad offices. Such as the seven men below Wei Fumin—their discussion of current government and pointing out omissions, though likes and dislikes often differed greatly, were all outstanding of the age. How much more the loyal purity of the brothers Yizhi and Ningzhi, and the literary drafting of Jiaoxiu and Chongli—there was also aid to governance and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In the Jianyan and Shaoxing era the court gathered outstanding men and spread them through every office. Wei Fumin and the six who follow debated policy and named failures; though their views often diverged, all stood among the age's finest. Especially the loyal integrity of Yizhi and Ningzhi and the draftsmanship of Jiaoxiu and Chongli—they too advanced governance and reform.
